The water in each of these oceans remains always the same in volume.

## \|\| 18.91-94 \|\|

*nyūnātiriktatā teṣāṃ kadācin naiva jāyate \|*  
*sthālīstham agnisaṃyogād udreki salilaṃ yathā \|\| 91 \|\|*

*tathenduvṛddhau salilam ambhodhau munisattamāḥ \|*  
*anyūnānatiriktāś ca vardhanty āpo hrasanti ca \|\| 92 \|\|*

*udayāstamane tv indoḥ pakṣayoḥ śuklakṛṣṇayoḥ \|*  
*daśottarāṇi pañcaiva aṅgulānāṃ śatāni ca \|\| 93 \|\|*

*apāṃ vṛddhikṣayau dṛṣṭau sāmudrīṇāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*bhojanaṃ puṣkaradvīpe tatra svayam upasthitam \|\| 94 \|\|*

91-94. They do not become less or more in the manner that water in a pot becomes less when heated by fire.

When the moon waxes, the water in the ocean does not increase. Waters move up or down in the same volume, neither more not less.

O excellent sages, during the moonrise and moonset in the two halves of the lunar month the waters of the ocean are seen moving up or down one thousand five hundred Aṅgulas.

The diet of the people in the Puṣkara Dvīpa comes to them by itself.

## \|\| 18.95-99 \|\|

*bhuñjanti ṣaḍrasaṃ viprāḥ prajāḥ sarvāḥ sadaiva hi \|*  
*svādūdakasya parito dṛśyate lokasaṃsthitiḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*dviguṇā kāñcanī bhūmiḥ sarvajantuvivarjitā \|*  
*lokālokas tataḥ śailo yojanāyutavistṛtaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*ucchrayeṇāpi tāvanti sahasrāṇy āvalohi saḥ \|*  
*tatas tamaḥ samāvṛtya taṃ śailaṃ sarvataḥ sthitam \|\| 97 \|\|*

*tamaś cāṇḍakaṭāhena samantāt pariveṣṭitam \|*  
*pañcāśatkoṭivistārā seyam urvī dvijottamāḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*sahaivāṇḍakaṭāhena sadvīpā samahīdharā \|*  
*seyaṃ dhātrī vidhātrī ca sarvabhūtaguṇādhikā \|*  
*ādhārabhūtā jagatāṃ sarveṣāṃ sā dvijottamāḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

95-99. O brahmins, there the subjects enjoy foodstuffs of all the six tastes always.

All round the ocean of sweet water a world is seen stationed. It is twice the size of the ocean. The ground is golden but devoid of all creatures.

Beyond that is the mountain Lokāloka extending to ten thousand Yojanas. That mountain is as many thousand Yojanas in height also.

Beyond that is darkness. It has encircled the mountain all round. That darkness is enveloped by the cauldron of the Egg (Aṇḍakaṭāha).

This universe extends to fifty crores of Yojanas along with the Aṇḍakaṭāha, Dvīpas, oceans and mountains.

O excellent brahmins, this earth is the support of all worlds. It is superior to all other creations, it is noble and excellent.

## Chapter 19 - The Magnitude of Netherworlds

## \|\| 19.1 \|\|

*lomaharṣaṇa uvāca:*  
*vistāra eṣa kathitaḥ pṛthivyā munisattamāḥ \|*  
*saptatis tu sahasrāṇi taducchrāyo 'pi kathyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

Lomaharṣaṇa said:

1\. O excellent sages, the extent of the Earth has been related. Its height (above the lowermost of the nether worlds) is said to be seventy-thousand Yojanas.

## \|\| 19.2-8 \|\|

*daśasāhasram ekaikaṃ pātālaṃ munisattamāḥ \|*  
*atalaṃ vitalaṃ caiva nitalaṃ sutalaṃ tathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*talātalaṃ rasātalaṃ pātālaṃ cāpi saptamam \|*  
*kṛṣṇā śuklāruṇā pītā śarkarā śailakāñcanī \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhūmayo yatra viprendrā varaprāsādaśobhitāḥ \|*  
*teṣu dānavadaiteya- jātayaḥ śataśaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nāgānāṃ ca mahāṅgānāṃ jñātayaś ca dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*svarlokād api ramyāṇi pātālānīti nāradaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prāha svargasadomadhye pātālebhyo gato divam \|*  
*āhlādakāriṇaḥ śubhrā maṇayo yatra suprabhāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*nāgābharaṇabhūṣāś ca pātālaṃ kena tatsamam \|*  
*daityadānavakanyābhir itaś cetaś ca śobhite \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pātāle kasya na prītir vimuktasyāpi jāyate \|*  
*divārkaraśmayo yatra prabhās tanvanti nātapam \|\| 8 \|\|*

2-8. O excellent sages, each one of the nether worlds is a thousand Yojanas above the lower one. The seven netherworlds are—Atala, Vitala, Nitala, Sutala, Talātala, Rasātala and Pātāla.

The grounds of these nether worlds are black, white, pink, yellow, gravelled, rocky and golden. O leading brahmins, excellent palaces adorn them.

In them the communities of Dānavas, Daityas and kins, men of Nāgas of huge bodies live, O excellent brahmins:

Nārada who entered the heavenly assembly coming straight to heaven from the nether regions said that the nether worlds were more charming than the heavenly world.

There are pure jewels of brilliant lustre which delight the onlookers. The ornaments of the Nāgas, the residents of the nether regions shine splendidly in heaven; there is nothing that is equal to it.

Who is not attracted and delighted by the right of nether regions which are rendered splendid by the lasses of Daityas and Dānavas? Even a liberated soul is drawn to it. During daytime, rays of the sun spread diffused light but not the glaring sunlight.

## \|\| 19.9-20 \|\|

*śaśinaś ca na śītāya niśi dyotāya kevalam \|*  
*bhakṣyabhojyamahāpāna- madamattaiś ca bhogibhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yatra na jñāyate kālo gato 'pi danujādibhiḥ \|*  
*vanāni nadyo ramyāṇi sarāṃsi kamalākarāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*puṃskokilādilāpāś ca manojñāny ambarāṇi ca \|*  
*bhūṣaṇāny atiramyāṇi gandhādyaṃ cānulepanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vīṇāveṇumṛdaṅgānāṃ niḥsvanāś ca sadā dvijāḥ \|*  
*etāny anyāni ramyāṇi bhāgyabhogyāni dānavaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*daityoragaiś ca bhujyante pātālāntaragocaraiḥ \|*  
*pātālānām adhaś cāste viṣṇor yā tāmasī tanuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śeṣākhyā yadguṇān vaktuṃ na śaktā daityadānavāḥ \|*  
*yo 'nantaḥ paṭhyate siddhair devadevarṣipūjitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sahasraśirasā vyaktaḥ svastikāmalabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*phaṇāmaṇisahasreṇa yaḥ sa vidyotayan diśaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sarvān karoti nirvīryān hitāya jagato 'surān \|*  
*madāghūrṇitanetro 'sau yaḥ sadaivaikakuṇḍalaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kirīṭī sragdharo bhāti sāgniśveta ivācalaḥ \|*  
*nīlavāsā madotsiktaḥ śvetahāropaśobhitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sābhragaṅgāprapāto 'sau kailāsādrir ivottamaḥ \|*  
*lāṅgalāsaktahastāgro bibhran muśalam uttamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*upāsyate svayaṃ kāntyā yo vāruṇyā ca mūrtayā \|*  
*kalpānte yasya vaktrebhyo viṣānalaśikhojjvalaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*saṃkarṣaṇātmako rudro niṣkramyātti jagattrayam \|*  
*sa bibhracchikharībhūtam aśeṣaṃ kṣitimaṇḍalam \|\| 20 \|\|*

9-20. During the night the light of the moon is not utilised for its coolness but only for illumination.

Since that passes away is not taken notice of by the Nāgas who enjoy with gaiety the foodstuffs and the edibles they consume and the great beverages they drink. Nor are Danujas and others aware of it.

O brahmins, the forests, rivers, lakes, and lotus ponds, the cooing of the cuckoo and other sweet birds, the pleasing skies, the unguents and the continuous notes and sounds of musical instruments such as the lute, flute and Mṛdaṅga drums, O brahmins—all these and other beautiful things are enjoyed by virtue of their good luck by Dānavas, Daityas and Nāgas residing in Pātāla. The Tāmasī form of Viṣṇu, named Śeṣa is beneath the lower regions.

Daityas and Dānavas are not capable of recountig his good qualities. He is honoured by Devas and celestial sages. He is spoken of as Ananta. He has a thousand hoods and he is clearly bedecked in Svastika ornaments devoid of impurities. He illuminates all quarters by thousand jewels on his hoods.

For the welfare of the universe he deprives the Asuras of their prowess. His eyes whirl and rove due to intoxication. He has only one earring at all times.

Wearing a crown and garlands he shines like a white mountain aflame with fire.

He is clad in blue garments. He is intoxicated with pride. He is resplendent with white garlands. He is lofty like the mountain of Kailāsa where the celestial Gaṅgā falls. He has placed his hand on the plough-share; he holds an excellent iron club. He is attended upon by the embodied splendour of Varuṇa.

At the end of the Kalpa, Rudra in the form of Saṅkarṣaṇa comes out of his mouth, blazing like the flame of poisonous fire and devours the three worlds.

He holds the entire sphere of the world rising above like a peak.

## \|\| 19.21-27 \|\|

*āste pātālamūlasthaḥ śeṣo 'śeṣasurārcitaḥ \|*  
*tasya vīryaṃ prabhāvaś ca svarūpaṃ rūpam eva ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nahi varṇayituṃ śakyaṃ jñātuṃ vā tridaśair api \|*  
*yasyaiṣā sakalā pṛthvī phaṇāmaṇiśikhāruṇā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*āste kusumamāleva kas tadvīryaṃ vadiṣyati \|*  
*yadā vijṛmbhate 'nanto madāghūrṇitalocanaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tadā calati bhūr eṣā sādritoyādhikānanā \|*  
*gandharvāpsarasaḥ siddhāḥ kiṃnaroragavāraṇāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*nāntaṃ guṇānāṃ gacchanti tato 'nanto 'yam avyayaḥ \|*  
*yasya nāgavadhūhastair lāpitaṃ haricandanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*muhuḥ śvāsānilāyastaṃ yāti dikpaṭavāsatām \|*  
*yam ārādhya purāṇarṣir gargo jyotīṃṣi tattvataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*jñātavān sakalaṃ caiva nimittapaṭhitaṃ phalam \|*  
*teneyaṃ nāgavaryeṇa śirasā vidhṛtā mahī \|*  
*bibharti sakalāṃl lokān sadevāsuramānuṣān \|\| 27 \|\|*

21-27. Worshipped by the entire hordes of Devas Śeṣa is stationed at the root of Pātāla. His prowess, power, form and features cannot be described or known even by the gods. The whole of the Earth is turned into pink by the flames of jewels on his hoods. It acts as a floral garland for Śeṣa. Who will be able to recount his prowess? When Śeṣa with his eyes rolling and roving due to intoxication, yawns and stretches himself, the whole of the Earth along with its rivers, forests and mountains, quakes and moves.

The Gandharvas, Apsaras, Siddhas, Kinnaras, Nāgas and Rākṣasas never reach the end of his good qualities. Hence, he is Ananta. He is unchanging. The Nāga lasses apply red sandal paste on him as unguent. Wafted by the wind of respiration it acts as the perfumed powder for the quarters. It was by propitiating him that the ancient sage Garga understood the luminaries factually and the predictive astrology based on omens.

The Earth is thus held on his head by the noble Nāga. He holds universe including Devas, Asuras and human beings.

## Chapter 20 - Hells in nether regions

## \|\| 20.1 \|\|

*lomaharṣaṇa uvāca:*  
*tataś cānantaraṃ viprā narakā rauravādayaḥ \|*  
*pāpino yeṣu pātyante tāñ śṛṇudhvaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Lomaharṣaṇa said:

1\. Thereafter, O brahmins, the hells are situated beneath the waters. The sinners are hurled down into them. Now, hear about them attentively, O excellent brahmins.

## \|\| 20.2-6 \|\|

*rauravaḥ śaukaro rodhas tāno viśasanas tathā \|*  
*mahājvālas taptakuḍyo mahālobho vimohanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*rudhirāndho vasātaptaḥ kṛmīśaḥ kṛmibhojanaḥ \|*  
*asipattravanaṃ kṛṣṇo lālābhakṣaś ca dāruṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tathā pūyavahaḥ pāpo vahnijvālo hy adhaḥśirāḥ \|*  
*sadaṃśaḥ kṛṣṇasūtraś ca tamaś cāvīcir eva ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śvabhojano 'thāpratiṣṭhoma- āvīciś ca tathāparaḥ \|*  
*ity evamādayaś cānye narakā bhṛśadāruṇāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yamasya viṣaye ghorāḥ śastrāgniviṣadarśinaḥ \|*  
*patanti yeṣu puruṣāḥ pāpakarmaratāś ca ye \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-6. They are Raurava, Śaukara, Rodha, Tāna, Viśasana, Mahājvāla, Taptakumbha, Mahālobha, Vimohana, Rudhirāndha, Vaitaraṇī, Kṛmīśa, Kṛmibhojana, Asipatravana, Kṛṣṇa, Lālabhakṣa, Pūyavaha, Papa, Vahnijvāla, Adhaḥśiras, Sadaṃśa, Kṛṣṇasūtra, Tamas, Avīci, Śvabhojana, Apratiṣṭha and a second Avīci. There are other similar hells extremely terrible which fall under the jurisdiction of Yama. They terrify by means of weapons and fires. The persons who are engaged in sinful activities fall into them.

## \|\| 20.7 \|\|

*kūṭasākṣī tathā samyak pakṣapātena yo vadet \|*  
*yaś cānyad anṛtaṃ vakti sa naro yāti rauravam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He who commits perjury, he who speaks with partiality and he who utters falsehood falls into Raurava hell.

## \|\| 20.8 \|\|

*bhrūṇahā purahantā ca goghnaś ca munisattamāḥ \|*  
*yānti te rauravaṃ ghoraṃ yaś cocchvāsanirodhakaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O excellent sages, he who destroys a foetus, he who murders his preceptor, he who slays cows and he who suffocates others—all these fall into terrible Raurava hell.

## \|\| 20.9 \|\|

*surāpo brahmahā hartā suvarṇasya ca śūkare \|*  
*prayāti narake yaś ca taiḥ saṃsargam upaiti vai \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He who drinks wine, he who slays a brahmin, he who steals gold and he who comes into contact with these—all these fall into Śūkara hell.

## \|\| 20.10 \|\|

*rājanyavaiśyahā caiva tathaiva gurutalpagaḥ \|*  
*taptakumbhe svasṛgāmī hanti rājabhaṭaṃ ca yaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He who murders a king, a Vaiśya and a royal soldier, he who defiles the bed of his preceptor and he who indulges in sexual intercourse with his sister—all these fall into Taptakumbha hell.

II. He who sells his chaste wife, he who keeps wine for sale, he who sells saffron, and he who discards a devoted friend or servant—all these fall into Taptaloha hell.

## \|\| 20.12-13 \|\|

*sutāṃ snuṣāṃ cāpi gatvā mahājvāle nipātyate \|*  
*avamantā gurūṇāṃ yo yaś cākroṣṭā narādhamaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vedadūṣayitā yaś ca vedavikrayakaś ca yaḥ \|*  
*agamyagāmī yaś ca syāt te yānti śabalaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. He who indulges in sexual intercourse with his daughter or daughter-in-law is hurled into Mahājvāla hell. He who insults preceptors and elders, he who reviles at them, he who slanders the Vedas, he who sells the Vedas and he who cohabits with the forbidden women falls into Sabala hell, O brahmins.

## \|\| 20.14-17 \|\|

*cauro vimohe patati maryādādūṣakas tathā \|*  
*devadvijapitṛdveṣṭā ratnadūṣayitā ca yaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sa yāti kṛmibhakṣye vai kṛmīśe tu duriṣṭikṛt \|*  
*pitṛdevātithīn yas tu paryaśnāti narādhamaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*lālābhakṣye sa yāty ugre śarakartā ca vedhake \|*  
*karoti karṇino yaś ca yaś ca khaḍgādikṛn naraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prayānty ete viśasane narake bhṛśadāruṇe \|*  
*asatpratigrahītā ca narake yāty adhomukhe \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. A thief falls into Vimoha hell, so also the person who defiles the line of demarcation of boundary.

He who hates Devas, brahmins and Pitṛs, he who spoils-jewels—falls into Kṛmibhakṣa hell.

He who performs an ill-conducted sacrifice falls into Kṛmīśa hell.

The base man who takes food prior to Pitṛs, Devas and guests falls into Lālābhakṣa hell. The maker of arrows falls into Vedhaka hell.

Those who make arrows with knots, those who make swords, and other destructive weapons fall into the terrible hell Víśasana.

He who receives gifts from indecent men falls into Adhomukha hell.

## \|\| 20.18 \|\|

*ayājyayājakas tatra tathā nakṣatrasūcakaḥ \|*  
*kṛmipūye naraś caiko yāti miṣṭānnabhuk sadā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He who performs a sacrifice on behalf of a person not entitled to that privilege, he who foretells by studying stars and he who partakes of sweet cooked food all by himself falls into Kṛmipūya hell.

## \|\| 20.19 \|\|

*lākṣāmāṃsarasānāṃ ca tilānāṃ lavaṇasya ca \|*  
*vikretā brāhmaṇo yāti tam eva narakaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O brahmins, the brahmin who sells lac, gravy, gingelly seeds and salt falls into the same hell.

## \|\| 20.20 \|\|

*mārjārakukkuṭacchāga- śvavarāhavihaṃgamān \|*  
*poṣayan narakaṃ yāti tam eva dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O excellent brahmins he who rears or eats poultry, goats, pigs and birds falls into the same hell.

## \|\| 20.21-22 \|\|

*raṅgopajīvī kaivartaḥ kuṇḍāśī garadas tathā \|*  
*sūcī māhiṣikaś caiva parvagāmī ca yo dvijaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*agāradāhī mitraghnaḥ śakunigrāmayājakaḥ \|*  
*rudhirāndhe patanty ete somaṃ vikrīṇate ca ye \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. He who subsists on the stage or the trade of fish, he who partakes of food from the hand of the bastard, he who administers poison, he who adopts the profession of a spy or a secret informer, he who rears buffaloes, or being a brahmin indulges in sexual intercourse on Parvan days, he who commits arson, he who hates friends, he who behaves as a deceptive and he who performs a sacrifice on behalf of all and sundry in the village and he who sells Soma juice falls into hell Rudhirandha.

## \|\| 20.23-24 \|\|

*madhuhā grāmahantā ca yāti vaitaraṇīṃ naraḥ \|*  
*retaḥpānādikartāro maryādābhedinaś ca ye \|\| 23 \|\|*

*te kṛcchre yānty aśaucāś ca kuhakājīvinaś ca ye \|*  
*asipattravanaṃ yāti vanacchedī vṛthaiva yaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. He who destroys honey, he who commits multi-murder of villagers falls into hell Vaitaraṇī.

Those who drink semen, those who break boundary lines or flout limits of decency, those who do not observe pollution (i.e. After birth of an infant or death of kinsman) and those who maintain themselves on deception fall into Kṛcchra hell. He who cuts off a forest in vain falls into hell Asipatravana.

## \|\| 20.25 \|\|

*aurabhrikā mṛgavyādhā vahnijvāle patanti vai \|*  
*yānti tatraiva te viprā yaś cāpākeṣu vahnidaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Those who hunt wild goats, sheep, or deer fall into hell Vahnijvāla. O brahmins, they too who burn things that should not be burnt, fall into hell.

## \|\| 20.26 \|\|

*vratopalopako yaś ca svāśramād vicyutaś ca yaḥ \|*  
*saṃdaṃśayātanāmadhye patatas tāv ubhāv api \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. He who commits omissions in the observance of holy rites and he who errs while performing duties of his stage (āśrama) fall into Sandaṃśa hell and endure its tortures.

## \|\| 20.27 \|\|

*divā svapneṣu syandante ye narā brahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*putrair adhyāpitā ye tu te patanti śvabhojane \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Those men and religious students who have vowed to celibacy but who discharge semen by day or during dreams, at night and those who are taught by their sons fall into Śvabhojana hell.

## \|\| 20.28 \|\|

*ete cānye ca narakāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*yeṣu duṣkṛtakarmāṇaḥ pacyante yātanāgatāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. These are the main hells, there are hundreds, and thousands of similar hells where the perpetrators of heinous crimes are cooked by day and night and tortured.

## \|\| 20.29 \|\|

*tathaiva pāpāny etāni tathānyāni sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*bhujyante jātipuruṣair narakāntaragocaraiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. These sins and thousands of similar sins are atoned for by men who are brought to suffering to one or other of these hells.

## \|\| 20.30 \|\|

*varṇāśramaviruddhaṃ ca karma kurvanti ye narāḥ \|*  
*karmaṇā manasā vācā nirayeṣu patanti te \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Those who act contrary to the tenets of disciplined life of Varṇas and Āśramas mentally, physically or verbally, fall into these hells.

## \|\| 20.31 \|\|

*adhaḥśirobhir dṛśyante nārakair divi devatāḥ \|*  
*devāś cādhomukhān sarvān adhaḥ paśyanti nārakān \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The gods in heaven are seen by the people of hells with their heads directed above. The gods see the residents of hells far below, their heads directed below.

## \|\| 20.32-33 \|\|

*sthāvarāḥ kṛmayo 'jvāś ca pakṣiṇaḥ paśavo narāḥ \|*  
*dhārmikās tridaśās tadvan mokṣiṇaś ca yathākramam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*sahasrabhāgaḥ prathamād dvitīyo 'nukramāt tathā \|*  
*sarve hy ete mahābhāgā yāvan muktisamāśrayāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. The following beings attain absolution in that order:—the immobile beings, worms, aquatic animals, birds, animals, men, righteous persons and Devas. The latter ones of these constitute a thousandth part of the former ones among them. All these, O highly blessed ones, progress till they achieve salvation.

## \|\| 20.34 \|\|

*yāvanto jantavaḥ svarge tāvanto narakaukasaḥ \|*  
*pāpakṛd yāti narakaṃ prāyaścittaparāṅmukhaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. There are as many dwellers in hell as there are creatures in heaven. He who commits sins but is averse to expiate for them, falls into hell.

## \|\| 20.35 \|\|

*pāpānām anurūpāṇi prāyaścittāni yad yathā \|*  
*tathā tathaiva saṃsmṛtya proktāni paramarṣibhiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Holy rites of expiation have been mentioned by great sages in proportion to sins. They have mentioned them being fully aware which particular expiation is capable of quelling the particular sin.

## \|\| 20.36 \|\|

*pāpe gurūṇi guruṇi svalpāny alpe ca tadvidaḥ \|*  
*prāyaścittāni viprendrā jaguḥ svāyaṃbhuvādayaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O leading brahmins, Manu and other sages have mentioned rites of atonement—elaborate ones if the sin is elaborate and minor ones if the sin is minor.

## \|\| 20.37 \|\|

*prāyaścittāny aśeṣāṇi tapaḥkarmātmakāni vai \|*  
*yāni teṣām aśeṣāṇāṃ kṛṣṇānusmaraṇaṃ param \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The acts of expiations are in the nature of austerities or holy rites. Of all of them the remembrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the most effective.

## \|\| 20.38 \|\|

*kṛte pāpe 'nutāpo vai yasya puṃsaḥ prajāyate \|*  
*prāyaścittaṃ tu tasyaikaṃ harisaṃsmaraṇaṃ param \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After committing a sin if a person repents for it, he should remember Viṣṇu—which is the sole rite of expiation for him. This is the greatest of all holy rites.

## \|\| 20.39 \|\|

*prātar niśi tathā saṃdhyā- madhyāhnādiṣu saṃsmaran \|*  
*nārāyaṇam avāpnoti sadyaḥ pāpakṣayān naraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Remembering Viṣṇu at dawn, night, dusk or midday the man attains Viṣṇu because his sins are immediately quelled.

## \|\| 20.40 \|\|

*viṣṇusaṃsmaraṇāt kṣīṇa- samastakleśasaṃcayaḥ \|*  
*muktiṃ prayāti bho viprā viṣṇos tasyānukīrtanāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. By remembering Viṣṇu his pains and strains perish immediately and they attain absolution. Attainment of heaven is an obstacle into him.

## \|\| 20.41 \|\|

*vāsudeve mano yasya japahomārcanādiṣu \|*  
*tasyāntarāyo viprendrā devendratvādikaṃ phalam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O leading brahmins, the benefits such as attaining the Status of Indra as a result of Japa, Homa, worship etc are obstacles to a man whose mind is set on Vāsudeva.

## \|\| 20.42 \|\|

*kva nākapṛṣṭhagamanaṃ punarāvṛttilakṣaṇam \|*  
*kva japo vāsudeveti muktibījam anuttamam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Where is the attainment of heaven characterised by a return once again to the Earth? Where is the Japa of Vāsudeva which is the most excellent cause of absolution (where there is no return to this earth)?

## \|\| 20.43 \|\|

*tasmād aharniśaṃ viṣṇuṃ saṃsmaran puruṣo dvijaḥ \|*  
*na yāti narakaṃ śuddhaḥ saṃkṣīṇākhilapātakaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Hence, no brahmin, no man, who remembers Viṣṇu day and night, falls into hell. If he has incurred sins they perish immediately.

## \|\| 20.44 \|\|

*manaḥprītikaraḥ svargo narakas tadviparyayaḥ \|*  
*narakasvargasaṃjñe vai pāpapuṇye dvijottamāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. That which delights the mind is heaven. That which is contrary in effect is hell. O excellent brahmins, good and evil are given the appellations of heaven and hell.

## \|\| 20.45 \|\|

*vastv ekam eva duḥkhāya sukhāyerṣyodayāya ca \|*  
*kopāya ca yatas tasmād vastu duḥkhātmakaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The one and the same object is conducive to misery as well as happiness. It produces malice and wrath. Hence there can never be an object solely of the nature of sorrow?

## \|\| 20.46 \|\|

*tad eva prītaye bhūtvā punar duḥkhāya jāyate \|*  
*tad eva kopālayataḥ prasādāya ca jāyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The same object generates pleasure at the outset, but later on, it yields misery. The same object causes pain, wrath but later on gives pleasure.

## \|\| 20.47 \|\|

*tasmād duḥkhātmakaṃ nāsti na ca kiṃcit sukhātmakam \|*  
*manasaḥ pariṇāmo 'yaṃ sukhaduḥkhādilakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Hence, there is nothing which is solely of the nature of sorrow or solely of the nature of pleasure. It is the changed phase of mind that is characterised by happiness or sorrow.

## \|\| 20.48 \|\|

*jñānam eva paraṃ brahmā- jñānaṃ bandhāya ceṣyate \|*  
*jñānātmakam idaṃ viśvaṃ na jñānād vidyate param \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Knowledge alone is the greatest Brahman; knowledge alone is effective for removing bondage. The universe is of the nature of knowledge. There is nothing greater than knowledge.

## \|\| 20.49-50 \|\|

*vidyāvidye hi bho viprā jñānam evāvadhāryatām \|*  
*evam etad mayākhyātaṃ bhavatāṃ maṇḍalaṃ bhuvaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*pātālāni ca sarvāṇi tathaiva narakā dvijāḥ \|*  
*samudrāḥ parvatāś caiva dvīpā varṣāṇi nimnagāḥ \|*  
*saṃkṣepāt sarvam ākhyātaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchatha \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. O brahmins let this be understood that knowledge alone is learning and ignorance.

Thus the sphere of Earth has been recounted to you by me. Similarly, O brahmins, I have recounted the nether regions, hells, oceans, mountains, continents subcontinents and rivers succinctly. Everything has been mentioned to you. What else do you desire to know?

## Chapter 21 - Upper Regions (Bhūr, Bhuvar, Svar etc.)

## \|\| 21.1-2 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ:*  
*kathitaṃ bhavatā sarvam asmākaṃ sakalaṃ tathā \|*  
*bhuvarlokādikāṃl lokāñ śrotum icchāmahe vayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tathaiva grahasaṃsthānaṃ pramāṇāni yathā tathā \|*  
*samācakṣva mahābhāga yathāval lomaharṣaṇa \|\| 2 \|\|*

The sages said:

1-2. Everything has been mentioned to us by you. We wish to know further about the upper worlds Bhūr, Bhuvar, Svar etc. “We also wish to know how the planets are stationed and what their magnitude is. O highly blessed Lomaharṣaṇa, mention these precisely.

## \|\| 21.3 \|\|

*lomaharṣaṇa uvāca:*  
*ravicandramasor yāvan mayūkhair avabhāsyate \|*  
*sasamudrasaricchailā tāvatī pṛthivī smṛtā \|\| 3 \|\|*

Lomaharṣaṇa said:

3\. That area which is illuminated by the rays of the sun and the moon is known as earth. It consists of oceans, rivers and mountains also.

## \|\| 21.4 \|\|

*yāvatpramāṇā pṛthivī vistāraparimaṇḍalā \|*  
*nabhas tāvatpramāṇaṃ hi vistāraparimaṇḍalam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The extent and magnitude of the sky is the same as those of the earth.

## \|\| 21.5 \|\|

*bhūmer yojanalakṣe tu sauraṃ viprās tu maṇḍalam \|*  
*lakṣe divākarāc cāpi maṇḍalaṃ śaśinaḥ sthitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O brahmins, the disc of the sun is stationed a hundred thousand Yojanas away from the earth. The disc of the moon is stationed a hundred thousand Yojanas away from the sun.

## \|\| 21.6 \|\|

*pūrṇe śatasahasre tu yojanānāṃ niśākarāt \|*  
*nakṣatramaṇḍalaṃ kṛtsnam upariṣṭāt prakāśate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Full hundred thousand Yojanas above the moon, the -entire sphere of the stars shines.

## \|\| 21.7 \|\|

*dvilakṣe cottare viprā budho nakṣatramaṇḍalāt \|*  
*tāvatpramāṇabhāge tu budhasyāpy uśanā sthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O brahmins, mercury (Budha) is two hundred thousand Yojanas above the sphere of stars. Venus (Uśanas) is stationed so many Yojanas above Mercury.

## \|\| 21.8 \|\|

*aṅgārako 'pi śukrasya tatpramāṇe vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*lakṣadvayena bhaumasya sthito devapurohitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Mars (Aṅgāraka) is stationed so many Yojanas above Venus. The preceptor of Devas, Jupiter, is stationed two hundred thousand Yojanas above Mars.

## \|\| 21.9 \|\|

*saurir bṛhaspater ūrdhvaṃ dvilakṣe samavasthitaḥ \|*  
*saptarṣimaṇḍalaṃ tasmāl lakṣam ekaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Saturn (Sauri) is stationed two hundred thousand Yojanas above Jupiter. The sphere of seven sages (the Great Bear), O excellent brahmins, is stationed a hundred thousand Yojanas beyond it.

## \|\| 21.10 \|\|

*ṛṣibhyas tu sahasrāṇāṃ śatād ūrdhvaṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*meḍhībhūtaḥ samastasya jyotiś cakrasya vai dhruvaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Polestar Dhruva that is the pivot of entire luminaries is stationed a hundred thousand Yojanas above seven sages.

## \|\| 21.11 \|\|

*trailokyam etat kathitaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*ijyāphalasya bhūr eṣā ijyā cātra pratiṣṭhitā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O excellent sages, the three worlds have been succinctly mentioned. This is the ground for the benefit of sacrifice. The sacrifice is established here.

## \|\| 21.12 \|\|

*dhruvād ūrdhvaṃ maharloko yatra te kalpavāsinaḥ \|*  
*ekayojanakoṭī tu maharloko vidhīyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Maharloka is a crore of Yojanas above Dhruva. It is here that the Kalpavāsins reside.

## \|\| 21.13 \|\|

*dve koṭyau tu jano loko yatra te brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*sanandanādyāḥ kathitā viprāś cāmalacetasaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Janaloka is two crores of Yojanas above Maharloka. It is here that Sanandana and other sons of Brahmā live. O brahmins, they are pure-minded.

## \|\| 21.14 \|\|

*caturguṇottaraṃ cordhvaṃ janalokāt tapaḥ smṛtam \|*  
*vairājā yatra te devāḥ sthitā dehavivarjitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Four times that distance above Janaloka (i.e. eight crores of Yojanas) is the Tapas region. It is there that the gods called Vairājas are stationed. They are devoid of physical forms.

## \|\| 21.15 \|\|

*ṣaḍguṇena tapolokāt satyaloko virājate \|*  
*apunarmārakaṃ yatra siddhādimunisevitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Six times that distance above the Tapas region (i.e. 48 crores of Yojanas) shines the Satyaloka. This region releases, one from the bondage of death (that which does not kill again) and is known as the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 21.16 \|\|

*pādagamyaṃ tu yat kiṃcid vastv asti pṛthivīmayam \|*  
*sa bhūrlokaḥ samākhyāto vistāro 'sya mayoditaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Wherever there is earthly ground or object that can be traversed by foot, it is called Bhurloka. Its extent has been mentioned by me.

## \|\| 21.17 \|\|

*bhūmisūryāntaraṃ yat tu siddhādimunisevitam \|*  
*bhuvarlokas tu so 'py ukto dvitīyo munisattamāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O excellent sages, the space between the earth and the sun, frequented by the sages, Siddhas and others, is called Bhuvarloka. It is the second of upper worlds.

## \|\| 21.18 \|\|

*dhruvasūryāntaraṃ yat tu niyutāni caturdaśa \|*  
*svarlokaḥ so 'pi kathito lokasaṃsthānacintakaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The space between Dhruva and the sun which extends to one million four hundred thousand Yojanas is said to be Svarloka by those who are conversant with the geography of the worlds.

## \|\| 21.19 \|\|

*trailokyam etat kṛtakaṃ vipraiś ca paripaṭhyate \|*  
*janas tapas tathā satyam iti cākṛtakaṃ trayam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. This set of three worlds is called Kṛtaka (artificial) by the brahmins. The three worlds Jana, Tapas and Satya are called Akṛtaka (Natural).

## \|\| 21.20 \|\|

*kṛtakākṛtako madhye maharloka iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*śūnyo bhavati kalpānte yo 'ntaṃ na ca vinaśyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In between the two, Maharloka is known as Kṛtakākṛtaka. At the end of a Kalpa it becomes empty but is not annihilated entirely.

## \|\| 21.21 \|\|

*ete sapta mahālokā mayā vaḥ kathitā dvijāḥ \|*  
*pātālāni ca saptaiva brahmāṇḍasyaiṣa vistaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O brahmins, these seven upper worlds have been mentioned by me to you as also the seven nether worlds. This is the detailed description of the cosmic Egg.

## \|\| 21.22 \|\|

*etad aṇḍakaṭāhena tiryag ūrdhvam adhas tathā \|*  
*kapitthasya yathā bījaṃ sarvato vai samāvṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. This is enveloped by the cauldron of the Egg (Aṇḍakaṭāha) all round, at the sides above and below like the seeds of an apple fruit.

## \|\| 21.23 \|\|

*daśottareṇa payasā dvijāś cāṇḍaṃ ca tad vṛtam \|*  
*sa cāmbuparivāro 'sau vahninā veṣṭito bahiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The Egg is enveloped by water ten times its size. The encircling volume of water is enveloped by fire.

## \|\| 21.24 \|\|

*vahnis tu vāyunā vāyur viprās tu nabhasāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*ākāśo 'pi muniśreṣṭhā mahatā pariveṣṭitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O brahmins, the fire is enveloped by wind; and the wind is enveloped by Ether. O excellent sages, the Ether is enveloped by Mahat.

## \|\| 21.25 \|\|

*daśottarāṇy aśeṣāṇi viprāś caitāni sapta vai \|*  
*mahāntaṃ ca samāvṛtya pradhānaṃ samavasthitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. These seven are such that the outer one is ten times, the size of the inner one..The Pradhāna stands enveloping the Mahat.

## \|\| 21.26 \|\|

*anantasya na tasyāntaḥ saṃkhyānaṃ cāpi vidyate \|*  
*tad anantam asaṃkhyātaṃ pramāṇenāpi vai yataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is infinite and endless. It has no reckoning since it cannot be measured by any unit, nor calculated by any figure.

## \|\| 21.27 \|\|

*hetubhūtam aśeṣasya prakṛtiḥ sā parā dvijāḥ \|*  
*aṇḍānāṃ tu sahasrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇy ayutāni ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O brahmins, it is the cause of entire creation. It is the great Prakṛti. There are thousands and thousands of such cosmic Eggs.

## \|\| 21.28-30 \|\|

*īdṛśānāṃ tathā tatra koṭikoṭiśatāni ca \|*  
*dāruṇy agnir yathā tailaṃ tile tadvat pumān iha \|\| 28 \|\|*

*pradhāne 'vasthito vyāpī cetanātmanivedanaḥ \|*  
*pradhānaṃ ca pumāṃś caiva sarvabhūtānubhūtayā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*viṣṇuśaktyā dvijaśreṣṭhā dhṛtau saṃśrayadharmiṇau \|*  
*tayoḥ saiva pṛthagbhāve kāraṇaṃ saṃśrayasya ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. There are eggs like these, crores and hundred crores in number.

Just as there is fire in the wood, or oil in the gingelly seed so also the Puruṣa is stationed in the Pradhāna which it provides. He is known as the conscious Ātman.

O excellent brahmins, the Pradhāna and the Puruṣa are sustained by the Energy of Viṣṇu that is the soul of all living beings. They mix together in their activity. Thus the energy of Viṣṇu alone is the cause of separation and integration of Puruṣa and Pradhāna.

## \|\| 21.31-36 \|\|

*kṣobhakāraṇabhūtā ca sargakāle dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*yathā śaityaṃ jale vāto bibharti kaṇikāgatam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*jagac chaktis tathā viṣṇoḥ pradhānapuruṣātmakam \|*  
*yathā ca pādapo mūla- skandhaśākhādisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ādyabījāt prabhavati bījāny anyāni vai tataḥ \|*  
*prabhavanti tatas tebhyo bhavanty anye pare drumāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*te 'pi tallakṣaṇadravya- kāraṇānugatā dvijāḥ \|*  
*evam avyākṛtāt pūrvaṃ jāyante mahadādayaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*viśeṣāntās tatas tebhyaḥ saṃbhavanti surādayaḥ \|*  
*tebhyaś ca putrās teṣāṃ tu putrāṇāṃ parame sutāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*bījād vṛkṣapraroheṇa yathā nāpacayas taroḥ \|*  
*bhūtānāṃ bhūtasargeṇa naivāsty apacayas tathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

31-36. O excellent sages, at the creation of the universe it is the cause of agitation.

Just as wind contains chillness of each and every drop of water so also the Energy of Viṣṇu contains both Pradhāna and Puruṣa together.

A tree with its roots, stem and branches grows out of the first seed. Many seeds come out of that thereafter. From those seeds grow other trees. These have the same characteristics, causes and parts.

In the same manner the Mahat etc are evolved, at the outset from the unevolved Pradhāna. From the Mahat to Viśeṣa this is the process of creation. Therefrom the gods and others are born. Their sons are born, their sons and grandsons. It goes on.

Just as there is no deficiency or decline in the tree due to the growth of another tree from its seeds so also the elements do not dwindle by the creation of other elements.

## \|\| 21.37 \|\|

*saṃnidhānād yathākāśa- kālādyāḥ kāraṇaṃ taroḥ \|*  
*tathaivāpariṇāmena viśvasya bhagavān hariḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Just as the Ether, time, etc. are as the cause of the tree by their mere presence, nearly so also Viṣṇu is the cause of universe without undergoing transformation.

## \|\| 21.38-40 \|\|

*vrīhibīje yathā mūlaṃ nālaṃ pattrāṅkurau tathā \|*  
*kāṇḍakoṣās tathā puṣpaṃ kṣīraṃ tadvac ca taṇḍulaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tuṣāḥ kaṇāś ca santo vai yānty āvirbhāvam ātmanaḥ \|*  
*prarohahetusāmagryam āsādya munisattamāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tathā karmasv anekeṣu devādyās tanavaḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*viṣṇuśaktiṃ samāsādya praroham upayānti vai \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. In the seed of a grain all these are present in latent form—viz—the root, stalk, sprout, leaf, stem, ovary, flower, milk (soup), rice-grain, husks and the bits of grain. O excellent sages, when all the complements of causes for the growth are present, these parts, already present within manifest themselves.

In the same manner, the physical forms of gods and human beings are already present in the diverse activities. They grow up, by coming into contact with the energy of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 21.41-44 \|\|

*sa ca viṣṇuḥ paraṃ brahma yataḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat \|*  
*jagac ca yo yatra cedaṃ yasmin vilayam eṣyati \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tad brahma paramaṃ dhāma sadasat paramaṃ padam \|*  
*yasya sarvam abhedena jagad etac carācaram \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sa eva mūlaprakṛtir vyaktarūpī jagac ca saḥ \|*  
*tasminn eva layaṃ sarvaṃ yāti tatra ca tiṣṭhati \|\| 43 \|\|*

*kartā kriyāṇāṃ sa ca ijyate kratuḥ \|*  
*sa eva tatkarmaphalaṃ ca tasya yat \|*  
*yugādi yasmāc ca bhaved aśeṣato \|*  
*harer na kiṃcid vyatiriktam asti tat \|\| 44 \|\|*

41-44. That Viṣṇu is the great Brahman from whom this universe evolves, in whom it subsists and in whom it is dissolved.

That Brahman is the greatest abode; and the great region beyond Sat and Asat. The universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings is identical with him.

He alone is the Primordial Nature. He alone is the universe when his form becomes manifest. In him alone everything is evolved and dissolved.

He is the agent of rites; he is worshipped; he alone is the sacrifice and the benefit thereof; he alone is the means of sacrifice. There is nothing which is separate and different from him.

## Chapter 22 - Pole Star (dhruva)

## \|\| 22.1 \|\|

*lomaharṣaṇa uvāca:*  
*tārāmayaṃ bhagavataḥ śiśumārākṛti prabhoḥ \|*  
*divi rūpaṃ harer yat tu tasya pucche sthito dhruvaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Lomaharṣaṇa said:

1\. Pole Star is situated at the tail end of the form of lord Viṣṇu in heaven which consists of constellations and which has the shape of Śiśumāra (the Gangetic porpoise).

## \|\| 22.2 \|\|

*saeṣa bhraman bhrāmayati candrādityādikān grahān \|*  
*bhramantam anu taṃ yānti nakṣatrāṇi ca cakravat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. He himself revolves and he makes the moon, sun and other planets too revolve. The constellations follow him in a circular orbit.

## \|\| 22.3 \|\|

*sūryācandramasau tārā nakṣatrāṇi grahaiḥ saha \|*  
*vātānīkamayair bandhair dhruve baddhāni tāni vai \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Along with the planets, the sun, moon, stars and constellations are tied to Dhruva by gaseous rows and lines.

## \|\| 22.4-5 \|\|

*śiśumārākṛti proktaṃ yad rūpaṃ jyotiṣāṃ divi \|*  
*nārāyaṇaḥ paraṃ dhāma tasyādhāraḥ svayaṃ hṛdi \|\| 4 \|\|*

*uttānapādatanayas tam ārādhya prajāpatim \|*  
*sa tārāśiśumārasya dhruvaḥ pucche vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Viṣṇu is the greatest abode. He is the support of that luminous form in heaven with the shape of Gangetic porpoise mentioned above.

(Meditating on the lord) in his heart, the son of Uttānapāda, Dhruva propitiated the Patriarch Brahmā and stationed himself at the tail end of the stellar Gangetic porpoise.

## \|\| 22.6 \|\|

*ādhāraḥ śiśumārasya sarvādhyakṣo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*dhruvasya śiśumāraś ca dhruve bhānur vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The support of Śiśumāra is Viṣṇu the presiding deity of all humanities. The Śiśumāra is the support of Dhruva and the sun is supported by Dhruva.

## \|\| 22.7 \|\|

*tad ādhāraṃ jagac cedaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|*  
*yena viprā vidhānena tan me śṛṇuta sāṃpratam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. This entire universe including Devas, Asuras and human beings is supported by the sun. O brahmins, now listen, by what method he supports the universe.

## \|\| 22.8 \|\|

*vivasvān aṣṭabhir māsair grasaty apo rasātmikāḥ \|*  
*varṣaty ambu tataś cānnam annādam akhilaṃ jagat \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. For eight months the sun absorbs water in the form of juice. Then he showers water in the form of rain. That gives rise to food-grains. This entire universe rests on food.

## \|\| 22.9-10 \|\|

*vivasvān aṃśubhis tīkṣṇair ādāya jagato jalam \|*  
*somaṃ puṣyaty athenduś ca vāyunāḍīmayair divi \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jalair vikṣipyate 'bhreṣu dhūmāgnyanilamūrtiṣu \|*  
*na bhraśyanti yatas tebhyo jalāny abhrāṇi tāny ataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. After absorbing water from the universe by his hot rays, the sun nourishes the moon. By the water-essence passing through the gaseous nerves the moon is held aloft over the clouds having their forms evolved out of smoke, fire and wind. The clouds are called Abhras because they hold waters and do not let them fall off.

## \|\| 22.11 \|\|

*abhrasthāḥ prapatanty āpo vāyunā samudīritāḥ \|*  
*saṃskāraṃ kālajanitaṃ viprāś cāsādya nirmalāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When nudged by the wind the waters in the clouds fall off. O brahmins, they attain the impressions of previous actions activised by the opportune time, and become pure.

## \|\| 22.12 \|\|

*saritsamudrā bhaumās tu tathāpaḥ prāṇisaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*catuṣprakārā bhagavān ādatte savitā dvijāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O brahmins, the sun-god absorbs four types of waters, viz. those of rivers, oceans, earth and those present in the living beings.

## \|\| 22.13-14 \|\|

*ākāśagaṅgāsalilaṃ tathāhṛtya gabhastimān \|*  
*anabhragatam evorvyāṃ sadyaḥ kṣipati raśmibhiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tasya saṃsparśanirdhūta- pāpapaṅko dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*na yāti narakaṃ martyo divyaṃ snānaṃ hi tat smṛtam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The multi-rayed sun absorbs water from the celestial Gaṅgā and immediately discharges it on to the earth without allowing it to get entangled with the clouds,

O excellent brahmins, the man who has washed the dirt of all sins due to his contact with it never falls into hell. Indeed, it is said to be a divine bath.

## \|\| 22.15 \|\|

*dṛṣṭasūryaṃ hi tad vāri pataty abhrair vinā divaḥ \|*  
*ākāśagaṅgāsalilaṃ tad gobhiḥ kṣipyate raveḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On seeing the sun, that water falls from heaven without the clouds acting as intermediary. That water from the celestial Gaṅgā is absorbed and cast off by the rays of the sun.

## \|\| 22.16 \|\|

*kṛttikādiṣu ṛkṣeṣu viṣameṣv ambu yad divaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvārkaṃ patitaṃ jñeyaṃ tad gāṅgaṃ diggajohnitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The water that falls from heaven on seeing the sun during Kṛttikā and other stars should be known as the water of Gaṅgā poured out by the elephants of quarters.

## \|\| 22.17 \|\|

*yugmarkṣeṣu tu yat toyaṃ pataty arkodgitaṃ divaḥ \|*  
*tat sūryaraśmibhiḥ sadyaḥ samādāya nirasyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The water that falls down during the even numbered (i.e. Rohiṇī, Ārdrā etc) from heaven after being absorbed by the sun is immediately scattered by the rays of the sun.

## \|\| 22.18 \|\|

*ubhayaṃ puṇyam atyarthaṃ nṛṇāṃ pāpaharaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*ākāśagaṅgāsalilaṃ divyaṃ snānaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O brahmins, both of them are extremely meritorious to human beings. They dispel sins. O excellent brahmins, one can have divine absolution with the waters of celestial Gaṅgā.

## \|\| 22.19 \|\|

*yat tu meghaiḥ samutsṛṣṭaṃ vāri tat prāṇināṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*puṣṇāty oṣadhayaḥ sarvā jīvanāyāmṛtaṃ hi tat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O brahmins, the water that is showered by the clouds nourishes living beings and makes the medicinal herbs grow well. It is the nectar that enlivens all.

## \|\| 22.20 \|\|

*tena vṛddhiṃ parāṃ nītaḥ sakalaś cauṣadhīgaṇaḥ \|*  
*sādhakaḥ phalapākāntaḥ prajānāṃ tu prajāyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. All kinds of medicinal plants increase thereby. Until they are mature and ripe they continue to be the means to the people.

## \|\| 22.21 \|\|

*tena yajñān yathāproktān mānavāḥ śāstracakṣuṣaḥ \|*  
*kurvate 'harahaś caiva devān āpyāyayanti te \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Day by day men with the sacred scriptures as their guides perform sacrifices in the manner they have been laid down and thereby nourish the gods.

## \|\| 22.22-23 \|\|

*evaṃ yajñāś ca vedāś ca varṇāś ca dvijapūrvakāḥ \|*  
*sarvadevanikāyāś ca paśubhūtagaṇāś ca ye \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vṛṣṭyā dhṛtam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*sāpi niṣpādyate vṛṣṭiḥ savitrā munisattamāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. The entire universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings is supported by rain. Thus the sacrifices, Vedas, castes beginning with the brahmins, Devas, animals and the rest of living beings—everyone is supported by rain. O excellent sages that rain is generated by the sun.

## \|\| 22.24 \|\|

*ādhārabhūtaḥ savitur dhruvo munivarottamāḥ \|*  
*dhruvasya śiśumāro 'sau so 'pi nārāyaṇāśrayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O excellent sages the support of the sun is the Polar Star and that of the Polar Star is Śiśumāra and that support of Śiśumāra is Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 22.25-26 \|\|

*hṛdi nārāyaṇas tasya śiśumārasya saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*vibhartā sarvabhūtānām ādibhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*evaṃ mayā muniśreṣṭhā brahmāṇḍaṃ samudāhṛtam \|*  
*bhūsamudrādibhir yuktaṃ kim anyac chrotum icchatha \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Viṣṇu is stationed in the heart of Śiśumāra. He maintains all living beings. He is the primordial cause and eternal.

Thus, O excellent sages, the cosmic egg has been cited by me along with the divisions of the earth, oceans etc. What else do you desire to know?

## Chapter 23 - Holy Centres (tīrtha): Their Greatness

## \|\| 23.1 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ:*  
*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni puṇyāny āyatanāni ca \|*  
*vaktum arhasi dharmajña śrotuṃ no vartate manaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. O Sūta conversent with piety, it behoves you to narrate the tale of holy shrines and centres over the earth. We are inclined to hear the same.

## \|\| 23.2 \|\|

*lomaharṣaṇa uvāca:*  
*yasya hastau ca pādau ca manaś caiva susaṃyatam \|*  
*vidyā tapaś ca kīrtiś ca sa tīrthaphalam aśnute \|\| 2 \|\|*

Lomaharṣaṇa said:

2\. He whose hands and feet are clean, whose mind is fully restrained and who has learning, penance and fame, enjoys the benefit of visiting holy shrines.

## \|\| 23.3 \|\|

*mano viśuddhaṃ puruṣasya tīrthaṃ \|*  
*vācāṃ tathā cendriyanigrahaś ca \|*  
*etāni tīrthāni śarīrajāni \|*  
*svargasya mārgaṃ pratibodhayanti \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The pure mind is the holy centre unto men. So also the control over speech and the restraint on the sense-organs. There are holy centres present in the physical body itself. They make the man understand the path of heaven.

## \|\| 23.4 \|\|

*cittam antargataṃ duṣṭaṃ tīrthasnānair na śudhyati \|*  
*śataśo 'pi jalair dhautaṃ surābhāṇḍam ivāśuci \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The wicked mind situated within does not become purified by ablutions in the sacred water in the holy centres, like the unclean mudpot of stale liquor which cannot become pure even when washed with water a hundred times.

## \|\| 23.5 \|\|

*na tīrthāni na dānāni na vratāni na cāśramāḥ \|*  
*duṣṭāśayaṃ dambharuciṃ punanti vyutthitendriyam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Neither holy centres, not charitable gifts nor holy rites, nor penance groves can purify the man whose mind is wicked, who takes delight in arrogance or who has not conquered his sense-organs.

## \|\| 23.6 \|\|

*indriyāṇi vaśe kṛtvā yatra yatra vasen naraḥ \|*  
*tatra tatra kurukṣetraṃ prayāgaṃ puṣkaraṃ tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Wherever a man stays after keeping his sense-organs fully under his control—the holy centres of Kurukṣetra, Prayāga and Puṣkara are present there.

## \|\| 23.7 \|\|

*tasmāc chṛṇudhvaṃ vakṣyāmi tīrthāny āyatanāni ca \|*  
*saṃkṣepeṇa muniśreṣṭhāḥ pṛthivyāṃ yāni kāni vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hence listen. I shall mention holy centres and sacred shrines—whatever there are on the earth, O excellent sages.

## \|\| 23.8-9 \|\|

*vistareṇa na śakyante vaktuṃ varṣaśatair api \|*  
*prathamaṃ puṣkaraṃ tīrthaṃ naimiṣāraṇyam eva ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*prayāgaṃ ca pravakṣyāmi dharmāraṇyaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*dhenukaṃ campakāraṇyaṃ saindhavāraṇyam eva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. They cannot be explained in detail even in the course of hundreds of years.

O excellent brahmins I shall mention holy centres of Puṣkara, Naimiśa forest, Prayāga and Dharmāraṇya as the foremost among holy spots.

There are Dhenuka, Campaka and Saindhava forests.

## \|\| 23.10 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ ca magadhāraṇyaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyam eva ca \|*  
*gayā prabhāsaṃ śrītīrthaṃ divyaṃ kanakhalaṃ tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The meritorious Sagarāraṇya forest, Daṇḍaka forest, Gaya, Prabhāsa, Śrītīrtha, and the divine Kanakhala.

## \|\| 23.11 \|\|

*bhṛgutuṅgaṃ hiraṇyākṣaṃ bhīmāraṇyaṃ kuśasthalīm \|*  
*lohākulaṃ sakedāraṃ mandarāraṇyam eva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Bhṛgutuṅga, Hiraṇyākṣa, Bhīmakanyā, Kuśasthalī, Lokārgala, Kedāra and Mandāra forest.

## \|\| 23.12 \|\|

*mahābalaṃ koṭitīrthaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ tathā \|*  
*rūpatīrthaṃ śūkaravaṃ cakratīrthaṃ mahāphalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Mahālaya, Koṭitīrtha, that dispels sins, Rūpatīrtha, Śūkara and Cakratīrtha of great benefit.

## \|\| 23.13 \|\|

*yogatīrthaṃ somatīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ sāhoṭakaṃ tathā \|*  
*tīrthaṃ kokāmukhaṃ puṇyaṃ badarīśailam eva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Vyāsatīrtha, Somatīrtha, Śākhoṭakatīrtha, Kokāmukha-tīrtha and the holy Badari mountain.

## \|\| 23.14 \|\|

*somatīrthaṃ tuṅgakūṭaṃ tīrthaṃ skandāśramaṃ tathā \|*  
*koṭitīrthaṃ cāgnipadaṃ tīrthaṃ pañcaśikhaṃ tathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Somatīrtha, Tuṅgakūṭa, Skandāśramatīrtha, Sūryaprabha, Dhenusaras and the seventh āyuṣmika.?

## \|\| 23.15 \|\|

*dharmodbhavaṃ koṭitīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ bādhapramocanam \|*  
*gaṅgādvāraṃ pañcakūṭaṃ madhyakesaram eva ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Koṭitīrtha at Dharmodbhava, the Sārva-kāmika-tīrtha, Sūryaprabha, Mahākuṇḍa and Somābhiṣecanatīrtha.

## \|\| 23.16 \|\|

*cakraprabhaṃ mataṅgaṃ ca kruśadaṇḍaṃ ca viśrutam \|*  
*daṃṣṭrākuṇḍaṃ viṣṇutīrthaṃ sārvakāmikam eva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Mahāśtotra, Koraka, Pañcadhāras Tridhāra, Saptadhāra, Ekadhāra and Amarakaṇṭakatīrtha.

## \|\| 23.17 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ matsyatilaṃ caiva badarī suprabhaṃ tathā \|*  
*brahmakuṇḍaṃ vahnikuṇḍaṃ tīrthaṃ satyapadaṃ tathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Śālagrāma, Cakratīrtha, the excellent Kadalīhrada, Vidyutprabha, Devahradatīrtha, and Viṣṇuprabha.

## \|\| 23.18 \|\|

*catuḥsrotaś catuḥśṛṅgaṃ śailaṃ dvādaśadhārakam \|*  
*mānasaṃ sthūlaśṛṅgaṃ ca sthūladaṇḍaṃ tathorvaśī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Śaṅkhaprabha, Devakuṇḍa, Vajrāyudhatīrtha, Vastrāpada, Barhapada and Lokārohaṇa.

## \|\| 23.19 \|\|

*lokapālaṃ manuvaraṃ somāhvaśailam eva ca \|*  
*sadāprabhaṃ merukuṇḍaṃ tīrthaṃ somābhiṣecanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Svayaṃvaṭa, Bhadrabala, Kauśāmba, Divākara, Sārasvata Dvīpa, Vijayadvīpa, and Kāmaja Dvīpa.

## \|\| 23.20 \|\|

*mahāsrotaṃ koṭarakaṃ pañcadhāraṃ tridhārakam \|*  
*saptadhāraikadhāraṃ ca tīrthaṃ cāmarakaṇṭakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. (?) Sollayāṅgopacāra, Cavarambana, Pūrṇavat (?) Snānakuṇḍa, Prayāga and Guhā Viṣṇupada.

## \|\| 23.21 \|\|

*śālagrāmaṃ cakratīrthaṃ koṭidrumam anuttamam \|*  
*bilvaprabhaṃ devahradaṃ tīrthaṃ viṣṇuhradaṃ tathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Kanyākuṇḍa, Vāyukuṇḍa, Jambūmārga the excellent holy centre, Gabhastitīrtha and the clean Yayāti Pattana.

## \|\| 23.22 \|\|

*śaṅkhaprabhaṃ devakuṇḍaṃ tīrthaṃ vajrāyudhaṃ tathā \|*  
*agniprabhaṃ ca puṃnāgaṃ devaprabham anuttamam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Bhadravaṭa Koṭitīrtha, Mahākālavana, the great Narmadātīrtha, Tīrthabīja and Arbuda.

## \|\| 23.23 \|\|

*vidyādharaṃ sagāndharvaṃ śrītīrthaṃ brahmaṇo hradam \|*  
*sātīrthaṃ lokapālākhyaṃ maṇipuragiriṃ tathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The Pañcatīrtha including Vasiṣṭhatīrtha, Priyasaṃjñaka, Vārṣika and the splendid Pañjiraka.

## \|\| 23.24 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ pañcahradaṃ caiva puṇyaṃ piṇḍārakaṃ tathā \|*  
*malavyaṃ goprabhāvaṃ ca govaraṃ vaṭamūlakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Sutīrtha, Brahmarudra, Kanyākumārika, Śakratīrtha,. Pañcanada and Reṇukātīrtha.

## \|\| 23.25 \|\|

*snānadaṇḍaṃ prayāgaṃ ca guhyaṃ viṣṇupadaṃ tathā \|*  
*kanyāśramaṃ vāyukuṇḍaṃ jambūmārgaṃ tathottamam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The pure Paitāmahatīrtha, the excellent Raudrapāda, Maṇimanta, Kāmākhya, Kṛṣṇatīrtha and Kuliṅgaka.

## \|\| 23.26 \|\|

*gabhastitīrthaṃ ca tathā yayātipatanaṃ śuci \|*  
*koṭitīrthaṃ bhadravaṭaṃ mahākālavanaṃ tathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Śrīśakrayajana, Brahmavālukā, the holy Vyāsatīrtha, Puṇḍarīka and the excellent Maṇimantha.

## \|\| 23.27 \|\|

*narmadātīrtham aparaṃ tīrthavajraṃ tathārbudam \|*  
*piṅgutīrthaṃ savāsiṣṭhaṃ tīrthaṃ ca pṛthasaṃgamam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Dīrghamantha, Haṃsapādatīrtha, Śayana, Daśāśvamedha, Kedāra and Tamasodbheda.

## \|\| 23.28 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ daurvāsikaṃ nāma tathā piñjarakaṃ śubham \|*  
*ṛṣitīrthaṃ brahmatuṅgaṃ vasutīrthaṃ kumārikam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Rudrakūpa, Saṃyamanītīrtha. Saṃtrāvanāsika, Syamantapañcaka, and Brahmatīrtha very pleasing to look.

## \|\| 23.29 \|\|

*śakratīrthaṃ pañcanadaṃ reṇukātīrtham eva ca \|*  
*paitāmahaṃ ca vimalaṃ rudrapādaṃ tathottamam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Pṛthivītīrtha, Pāriplava, Pṛthūdaka, Daśāśvamedhika, Sākṣida and Vijaya.

## \|\| 23.30 \|\|

*maṇimattaṃ ca kāmākhyaṃ kṛṣṇatīrthaṃ kuśāvilam \|*  
*yajanaṃ yājanaṃ caiva tathaiva brahmavālukam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The Koṭitīrtha at Pañcanada, Varāha, Yakṣiṇīhrada, Puṇḍarīka, Somatīrtha, and the excellent Muñjāvaṭaratha.

## \|\| 23.31 \|\|

*puṣpanyāsaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ maṇipūraṃ tathottaram \|*  
*dīrghasattraṃ hayapadaṃ tīrthaṃ cānaśanaṃ tathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Babūravanatīrtha situated in the forest Badarīvana, Svarlokadvāraka and Kapilātīrtha.

## \|\| 23.32 \|\|

*gaṅgodbhedaṃ śivodbhedaṃ narmadodbhedam eva ca \|*  
*vastrāpadaṃ dāruvalaṃ chāyārohaṇam eva ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Sūryatīrtha, Varusthāna, Bhavābhavana, Yakṣarākṣasatīrtha, and Brahmatīrtha the excellent holy centre.

## \|\| 23.33 \|\|

*siddheśvaraṃ mitravalaṃ kālikāśramam eva ca \|*  
*vaṭāvaṭaṃ bhadravaṭaṃ kauśāmbī ca divākaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Kāmeśvara, Mātṛtīrtha, Śātavana, the abode of the earthly Haṃsa (swan) and the Sārasatīrtha.

## \|\| 23.34 \|\|

*dvīpaṃ sārasvataṃ caiva vijayaṃ kāmadaṃ tathā \|*  
*rudrakoṭiṃ sumanasaṃ tīrthaṃ sadrāvanāmitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Daśāśvamedha, Kedāra, excellent Brahmajña Saptarṣikuṇḍa and the well-delimited tīrtha of the goddess.

## \|\| 23.35 \|\|

*syamantapañcakaṃ tīrthaṃ brahmatīrthaṃ sudarśanam \|*  
*satataṃ pṛthivīsarvaṃ pāriplavapṛthūdakau \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Ihāspada (the support here, on earth) Koṭikṛta, Kiṃvāna, Kiṃjaya, Kāraṇḍava, Viśvatīrtha and another Triviṣṭapatīrtha.

## \|\| 23.36 \|\|

*daśāśvamedhikaṃ tīrthaṃ sarpijaṃ viṣayāntikam \|*  
*koṭitīrthaṃ pañcanadaṃ vārāhaṃ yakṣiṇīhradam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Pāṇikhātatīrtha, Miśrakatīrtha, Madhukaṇṭatīrtha, Manomayatīrtha, the divine Kauśikītīrtha and the excellent Kanyātīrtha.

## \|\| 23.37 \|\|

*puṇḍarīkaṃ somatīrthaṃ muñjavaṭaṃ tathottamam \|*  
*badarīvanam āsīnaṃ ratnamūlakam eva ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The Brahmatīrtha, Manastīrtha, the sacred holy centre, Saugandhika the holy forest, Maṇitīrtha and Sarasvatītīrtha.

## \|\| 23.38 \|\|

*lokadvāraṃ pañcatīrthaṃ kapilātīrtham eva ca \|*  
*sūryatīrthaṃ śaṅkhinī ca gavāṃ bhavanam eva ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The most excellent holy centre Īśānatīrtha, the holy Pañcayajñaka, Triśūladhara, Mahendra, and the divine abode Mahālaya,

## \|\| 23.39 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ ca yakṣarājasya brahmāvartaṃ sutīrthakam \|*  
*kāmeśvaraṃ mātritīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ śītavanaṃ tathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The divine holy centre Śākambharītīrtha, Suvarṇākhya, Kapīmada, Kṣīreśvara, Virūpākṣa, Bhṛgutīrtha and Kuśodbhava.

## \|\| 23.40 \|\|

*snānalomāpahaṃ caiva māsasaṃsarakaṃ tathā \|*  
*daśāśvamedhaṃ kedāraṃ brahmodumbaram eva ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Brahmāvarta, Brahmayoni, the mountain Nīlaparvata, the eddy Bhadrakarṇa and the eddy Śakrakarṇa.

## \|\| 23.41 \|\|

*saptarṣikuṇḍaṃ ca tathā tīrthaṃ devyāḥ sujambukam \|*  
*īṭāspadaṃ koṭikūṭaṃ kiṃdānaṃ kiṃjapaṃ tathā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Saptasārasvata, the holy centre of Auśanasatīrtha, Kapālamocana, Avakīrṇa and Pañcakatīrtha.

## \|\| 23.42 \|\|

*kāraṇḍavaṃ cāvedhyaṃ ca triviṣṭapam athāparam \|*  
*pāṇiṣātaṃ miśrakaṃ ca madhūvaṭamanojavau \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Catussāmudrika, Satkāñcanasahasrika, Reṇuka, Pañcakaṭaka and Ainasa-Vimocanatīrtha.

## \|\| 23.43 \|\|

*kauśikī devatīrthaṃ ca tīrthaṃ ca ṛṇamocanam \|*  
*divyaṃ ca nṛgadhūmākhyaṃ tīrthaṃ viṣṇupadaṃ tathā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Sthāṇutīrtha, Tīrtha of Kuru, Svargadvāra, Kuśadhvaja, Viśveśvara, Vāmakara and the hermitage of Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 23.44 \|\|

*amarāṇāṃ hradaṃ puṇyaṃ koṭitīrthaṃ tathāparam \|*  
*śrīkuñjaṃ śālitīrthaṃ ca naimiṣeyaṃ ca viśrutam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Gaṅgāhrada, the holy Vaṭa and Badarī, Indramārgaṇakṣetra and Jirikāvāsa.

## \|\| 23.45 \|\|

*brahmasthānaṃ somatīrthaṃ kanyātīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*brahmatīrthaṃ manastīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ vai kārupāvanam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. O brahmins, Somatīrtha, the meritorious Koṭitīrtha, the holy spot of Koṭitīrthasthalī, an eddy by Bhadrakālī.

## \|\| 23.46 \|\|

*saugandhikavanaṃ caiva maṇitīrthaṃ sarasvatī \|*  
*īśānatīrthaṃ pravaraṃ pāvanaṃ pāñcayajñikam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The holy forest of Arundhatīvana, the excellent Brahmāvarta, Aśvadevī, Kubjavana and Yamunāprabhava.

## \|\| 23.47 \|\|

*triśūladhāraṃ māhendraṃ devasthānaṃ kṛtālayam \|*  
*śākaṃbharī devatīrthaṃ suvarṇākhyaṃ kilaṃ hradam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Vīra-Pramokṣa, Siddhārtha, Māyāvidyodbhava, Mahāhrada, Vetasikārūpa and Sundarikāśrama.

## \|\| 23.48 \|\|

*kṣīraśravaṃ virūpākṣaṃ bhṛgutīrthaṃ kuśodbhavam \|*  
*brahmatīrthaṃ brahmayoniṃ nīlaparvatam eva ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Brahmāṇītīrtha, which is very great, Gaṅgodbhavasarasvatī, Bāhukātīrtha and Vimalāśokatīrtha.

## \|\| 23.49 \|\|

*kubjāmbakaṃ bhadravaṭaṃ vasiṣṭhapadam eva ca \|*  
*svargadvāraṃ prajādvāraṃ kālikāśramam eva ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Gautamītīrtha, Airāvatītīrtha, Śatasahasrikātīrtha, Koṭitīrtha in the abode Bhartṛsthāna and the excellent Kāpilītīrtha.

## \|\| 23.50 \|\|

*rudrāvartaṃ sugandhāśvaṃ kapilāvanam eva ca \|*  
*bhadrakarṇahradaṃ caiva śaṅkukarṇahradaṃ tathā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The Pañcanadatīrtha of the intelligent Mārkaṇḍeya, Somatīrtha, Śivoda and Matsyodarītīrtha.

## \|\| 23.51 \|\|

*saptasārasvataṃ caiva tīrtham auśanasaṃ tathā \|*  
*kapālamocanaṃ caiva avakīrṇaṃ ca kāmyakam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Sūryatīrtha having the lustre of the sun, the holy forest Somakavana, Aruṇāspada, Vāmanaka and the Sūryatīrtha abounding in sands.

## \|\| 23.52 \|\|

*catuḥsāmudrikaṃ caiva śatakiṃ ca sahasrikam \|*  
*reṇukaṃ pañcavaṭakaṃ vimocanam athaujasam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The Tīrtha called Avimukta, the Nīlakaṇṭhahrada, Piśācamocana, and Subhadrāhrada.

## \|\| 23.53 \|\|

*sthāṇutīrthaṃ kuros tīrthaṃ svargadvāraṃ kuśadhvajam \|*  
*viśveśvaraṃ mānavakaṃ kūpaṃ nārāyaṇāśrayam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Vimalakuṇḍa, Tīrtha of Caṇḍīśvara, Śreṣṭhasthānahrada and Samudrakūpa.

## \|\| 23.54 \|\|

*gaṅgāhradaṃ vaṭaṃ caiva badarīpāṭanaṃ tathā \|*  
*indramārgam ekarātraṃ kṣīrakāvāsam eva ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The forest of Jaigīṣavya, the forest of Hṛṣīkeśa, Ajāmukharasa, and the whirlpool of Ghaṇṭākarṇa.

## \|\| 23.55 \|\|

*somatīrthaṃ dadhīcaṃ ca śrutatīrthaṃ ca bho dvijāḥ \|*  
*koṭitīrthasthalīṃ caiva bhadrakālīhradaṃ tathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Puṇḍarīkahrada, the tank of Kāṣṭhaka, Śmaśānastambha, Kumbhatīrtha and the Vināyakahrada.

## \|\| 23.56 \|\|

*arundhatīvanaṃ caiva brahmāvartaṃ tathottamam \|*  
*aśvavedī kubjāvanaṃ yamunāprabhavaṃ tathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The well born of the Siddhas, the holy lake Brahmasaras Bhadrāvāsa, Nāgatīrtha and Somatīrtha.

## \|\| 23.57 \|\|

*vīraṃ pramokṣaṃ sindhūttham ṛṣa kulyā sakṛttikam \|*  
*urvīsaṃkramaṇaṃ caiva māyāvidyodbhavaṃ tathā \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Bhaktahrada, the lake of milk, Pretādhāra, Kumārakatīrtha, Brahmāvarta Kuśāvarta and the holy centre Dadhikarṇodaya.

## \|\| 23.58 \|\|

*mahāśramo vaitasikā- rūpaṃ sundarikāśramam \|*  
*bāhutīrthaṃ cārunadīṃ vimalāśokam eva ca \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The great holy centre of Śṛṇgatīrtha, the excellent holy centre of Mahānadī, the divine lake Brahmasaras, and the holy Akṣayavaṭa at Gayāśīrṣa.

## \|\| 23.59 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ pañcanadaṃ caiva mārkaṇḍeyasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*somatīrthaṃ sitodaṃ ca tīrthaṃ matsyodarīṃ tathā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Gomayatīrtha in the South, Hayaśāntika in the north, Kapilāhrada, Gṛdhrakūṭa and Sāvitrīhrada.

## \|\| 23.60 \|\|

*sūryaprabhaṃ sūryatīrtham aśokavanam eva ca \|*  
*aruṇāspadaṃ kāmadaṃ ca śukratīrthaṃ savālukam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The forest Gītavana that destroys sins, Yonidvāra, Dhainuka, Dhanvaka, Lohika and Mataṅgahrada.

## \|\| 23.61 \|\|

*piśācamocanaṃ caiva subhadrāhradam eva ca \|*  
*kuṇḍaṃ vimaladaṇḍasya tīrthaṃ caṇḍeśvarasya ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Pitṛkūpa, Rudrakūpa, Matitīrtha, Sumālin, Brahmasthāna, Saptakuṇḍa, and Maṇiratnahrada.

## \|\| 23.62 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhasthānahradaṃ caiva puṇyaṃ brahmasaraṃ tathā \|*  
*jaigīṣavyaguhā caiva harikeśavanaṃ tathā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The hermitage of Mudgala, the whirlpool of Mudgala, the holy centre Janakakūpa, and the holy Tīrtha Vinaśana.

## \|\| 23.63 \|\|

*ajāmukhasaraṃ caiva ghaṇṭākarṇahradaṃ tathā \|*  
*puṇḍarīkahradaṃ caiva vāpī karkoṭakasya ca \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The holy centre Śoka, Bhāratatīrtha, Jyeṣṭhālika, Viśveśvara of hundredfold merits, and Kanyāsaṃvedha.

## \|\| 23.64 \|\|

*suvarṇasyodapānaṃ ca śvetatīrthahradaṃ tathā \|*  
*kuṇḍaṃ ghargharikāyāś ca śyāmakūpaṃ ca candrikā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Nidhitīrtha, Rāmabhavatīrtha, the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha, Devakūṭa, Devakūpa and the hermitage of Kauśika.

## \|\| 23.65 \|\|

*śmaśānastambhakūpaṃ ca vināyakahradaṃ tathā \|*  
*kūpaṃ sindhūdbhavaṃ caiva puṇyaṃ brahmasaraṃ tathā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Kulakarṇahrada, Kauśikīdruma, Dharmatīrtha, Kāñcanatīrtha and the holy centre Uddālaka.

## \|\| 23.66 \|\|

*rudrāvāsaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ nāgatīrthaṃ pulomakam \|*  
*bhaktahradaṃ kṣīrasaraḥ pretādhāraṃ kumārakam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Daṇḍātmā, Mālinītīrtha, Vanacaṇḍikātīrtha, Sandhyātīrtha, Kālatīrtha, Kapilātīrtha and Lohitārṇava.

## \|\| 23.67 \|\|

*brahmāvartaṃ kuśāvartaṃ dadhikarṇodapānakam \|*  
*śṛṅgatīrthaṃ mahātīrthaṃ tīrthaśreṣṭhā mahānadī \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Śoṇodbhava, Vaṃśagulma, the centre of Rāma Bhaṅgīka, Puṇyāvartahrada, Śrīmattīrtha and the hermitage Badarikāśrama.

## \|\| 23.68 \|\|

*divyaṃ brahmasaraṃ puṇyaṃ gayāśīrṣākṣayaṃ vaṭam \|*  
*dakṣiṇaṃ cottaraṃ caiva gomayaṃ rūpaśītikam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Rāmatīrtha, Vitastā, Merujātīya, the Rohiṇī and the lake of Indradyumna.

## \|\| 23.69 \|\|

*kapilāhradaṃ gṛdhravaṭaṃ sāvitrīhradam eva ca \|*  
*prabhāsanaṃ sītavanaṃ yonidvāraṃ ca dhenukam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Avasarga, Mahendra, Śrītīrtha and the holy centre Iṣutīrtha, Vārṣika, and the abode of Kubera.

## \|\| 23.70 \|\|

*dhanyakaṃ kokilākhyaṃ ca mataṅgahradam eva ca \|*  
*pitṛkūpaṃ rudratīrthaṃ śakratīrthaṃ sumālinam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Kanyātīrtha, Gokarṇa, the abode, of Gopati Saṃvarta, Viśvāsa and the group of seven deep pools named Saptagodāvarīhrada.

## \|\| 23.71 \|\|

*brahmasthānaṃ saptakuṇḍaṃ maṇiratnahradaṃ tathā \|*  
*kauśikyaṃ bharataṃ caiva tīrthaṃ jyeṣṭhālikā tathā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Another Badarīhrada, Brahmasthānavivardhana, Jātihrada, Devahrada, and Kuśaprathana.

## \|\| 23.72 \|\|

*viśveśvaraṃ kalpasaraḥ kanyāsaṃvetyam eva ca \|*  
*niścīvā prabhavaś caiva vasiṣṭhāśramam eva ca \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Sarvadevavrata, Kanyāśramahrada, Mahārājahrada, the holy Śakratīrtha and Kundaka.

## \|\| 23.73 \|\|

*devakūṭaṃ ca kūpaṃ ca vasiṣṭhāśramam eva ca \|*  
*vīrāśramaṃ brahmasaro brahmavīrāvakāpilī \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Āṅgāratīrtha, the forest Rudrāraṇyaka, Medhāvin, Devahrada and the holy centre Amaravartana.

## \|\| 23.74 \|\|

*kumāradhārā śrīdhārā gaurīśikharam eva ca \|*  
*śunaḥ kuṇḍo 'tha tīrthaṃ ca nanditīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The holy Mandākinīhrada, Kṣama, Māheśvara, Gaṅgātīrtha, Tripuruṣa, and Bhīmatāṇḍavamukha.

## \|\| 23.75 \|\|

*kumāravāsaṃ śrīvāsam aurvīśītārtham eva ca \|*  
*kumbhakarṇahradaṃ caiva kauśikīhradam eva ca \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Pṛthukūṭa, Śālvakūṭa, Śoṇa, Rohitaka, Kapilahrada, Mālya and Kapilāhrada belonging to Vasiṣṭha.

## \|\| 23.76-79 \|\|

*dharmatīrthaṃ kāmatīrthaṃ tīrtham uddālakaṃ tathā \|*  
*saṃdhyātīrthaṃ kāratoyaṃ kapilaṃ lohitārṇavam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*śoṇodbhavaṃ vaṃśagulmam ṛṣabhaṃ kalatīrthakam \|*  
*puṇyāvatīhradaṃ tīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ badarikāśramam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*rāmatīrthaṃ pitṛvanaṃ virajātīrtham eva ca \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyavanaṃ caiva kṛṣṇatīrthaṃ tathā vaṭam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*rohiṇīkūpapravaram indradyumnasaraṃ ca yat \|*  
*sānugartaṃ samāhendraṃ śrītīrthaṃ śrīnadaṃ tathā \|\| 79 \|\|*

76-79. The eddies, the holy waterspots of Vālakhilyas, the seven sages, other great sages and the Akhaṇḍita-hrada.

The man who is endowed with faith who lakes his bath duly in these sacred water spots and holy centres should observe fast and control his sense-organs. He should perform Tarpaṇa rites for Devas, sages and Pitṛs. After worshipping the deities he should stay there for three nights.

O brahmins, benefits are derived severally from each of these holy centres. Undoubtedly, the man obtains the benefit of a horse-sacrifice by making journeys to these places.

He who listens to this narrative daily, or who narrates this greatness of holy centres is liberated from sins.

## Chapter 24 - A Dialogue between Brahmā and Sages

## \|\| 24.1 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ:*  
*pṛthivyām uttamāṃ bhūmiṃ dharmakāmārthamokṣadām \|*  
*tīrthānām uttamaṃ tīrthaṃ brūhi no vadatāṃ vara \|\| 1 \|\|*

The sages said:

1\. O Sūta the most excellent among the eloquent ones, tell us about the most excellent place on earth, that bestows virtue, love, wealth and salvation and that is the most excellent of all holy centres.

## \|\| 24.2 \|\|

*lomaharṣaṇa uvāca:*  
*imaṃ praśnaṃ mama guruṃ papracchur munayaḥ purā \|*  
*tam ahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yat pṛcchadhvaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Lomaharṣaṇa said:

2\. O excellent brahmins formerly, the great sages asked my preceptor this very question that you ask me just now. I shall mention it.

## \|\| 24.3-8 \|\|

*svāśrame sumahāpuṇye nānāpuṣpopaśobhite \|*  
*nānādrumalatākīrṇe nānāmṛgagaṇair yute \|\| 3 \|\|*

*puṃnāgaiḥ karṇikāraiś ca saralair devadārubhiḥ \|*  
*śālais tālais tamālaiś ca panasair dhavakhādiraiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pāṭalāśokabakulaiḥ karavīraiḥ sacampakaiḥ \|*  
*anyaiś ca vividhair vṛkṣair nānāpuṣpopaśobhitaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kurukṣetre samāsīnaṃ vyāsaṃ matimatāṃ varam \|*  
*mahābhāratakartāraṃ sarvaśāstraviśāradam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*adhyātmaniṣṭhaṃ sarvajñaṃ sarvabhūtahite ratam \|*  
*purāṇāgamavaktāraṃ vedavedāṅgapāragam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*parāśarasutaṃ śāntaṃ padmapattrāyatekṣaṇam \|*  
*draṣṭum abhyāyayuḥ prītyā munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

3-8. My preceptor Vyāsa, the holy sage was seated in his hermitage in Kurukṣetra. The hermitage was rendered splendid by different varieties of flowers. It abounded in different kinds of trees, creepers and herds of different animals. There were the following trees—Punnāga, Karṇikāra, Sarala, Devadāru, Śāla, Tāla, Tamāla Panasa, Khadira, Pāṭala, Aśoka, Bakula, Karavīra, Campaka and other trees, all in full bloom. My preceptor was an expert in sacred scriptures. He had composed the great Mahābhārata. He was the foremost among intellectuals. He was omniscient and engaged in activities conducive to the welfare of all living beings. He was engrossed in spiritual quests. He had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. He had expounded the Purāṇas and Āgamas. He was the son of Parāśara. He was handsome with eyes as wide as the petals of the lotus.

The sages of holy rites came there to see the calm sage.

## \|\| 24.9-14 \|\|

*kaśyapo jamadagniś ca bharadvājo 'tha gautamaḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭho jaiminir dhaumyo mārkaṇḍeyo 'tha vālmikiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*viśvāmitraḥ śatānando vātsyo gārgyo 'tha āsuriḥ \|*  
*sumantur bhārgavo nāma kaṇvo medhātithir guruḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*māṇḍavyaś cyavano dhūmro hy asito devalas tathā \|*  
*maudgalyas tṛṇayajñaś ca pippalādo 'kṛtavraṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*saṃvartaḥ kauśiko raibhyo maitreyo haritas tathā \|*  
*śāṇḍilyaś ca vibhāṇḍaś ca durvāsā lomaśas tathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nāradaḥ parvataś caiva vaiśaṃpāyanagālavau \|*  
*bhāskariḥ pūraṇaḥ sūtaḥ pulastyaḥ kapilas tathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ulūkaḥ pulaho vāyur devasthānaś caturbhujaḥ \|*  
*sanatkumāraḥ pailaś ca kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇānubhautikaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

9-14. The following were the sages who came viz.—Kaśyapa, Jamadagni, Bharadvāja, Gautama, Vasiṣṭha, Jaimini, Dhaumya, Mārkaṇḍeya,Vālmīki, Viśvāmitra, Śatānanda,Vātsya, Garga, Āsuri, Sumantu, Bhārgava, Kaṇva, Medhātithi, Guru Māṇḍavya, Cyavana, Dhūmra, Asita, Devala, Maudgalya, Tṛṇabāhu, Pippalāda, Akṛtavraṇa, Saṃvarta, Kauśika, Raibhya, Maitreya, Hārīta, Śāṇḍilya, Agastya, Durvāsas, Lomaśa, Nārada, Parvata, Vaiśampāyana, Gālava, Bhāskari, Pūraṇi, Sūta, Pulastya, Ulūka, Pulaha, Vāyu, Devasthāna, Tumburu, Sanatkumāra, Paila, Kṛṣṇa and Kṛṣṇānubhautika.

## \|\| 24.15 \|\|

*etair munivaraiś cānyair vṛtaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ \|*  
*rarāja sa muniḥ śrīmān nakṣatrair iva candramāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The intelligent sage, son of Satyavatī surrounded by these and other excellent sages shone like the moon surrounded by the stars.

## \|\| 24.16 \|\|

*tān āgatān munīn sarvān pūjayām āsa vedavit \|*  
*te 'pi taṃ pratipūjyaiva kathāṃ cakruḥ parasparam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The sage, the knower of the Vedas honoured those sages who came there. They too honoured him in return. Thereafter, they engaged themselves in conversation.

## \|\| 24.17 \|\|

*kathānte te muniśreṣṭhāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ satyavatīsutam \|*  
*papracchuḥ saṃśayaṃ sarve tapovananivāsinaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. At the end of their preliminary talk the excellent sages, the residents of the penance-groves asked Kṛṣṇa (Dvaipāyana), the son of Satyavatī to clarify their doubts.

## \|\| 24.18 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ:*  
*mune vedāṃś ca śāstrāṇi purāṇāgamabhāratam \|*  
*bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca sarvaṃ jānāsi vāṅmayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

The sages said:

18\. O sage, you know the entire range of sacred lore, viz, the Vedas, Purāṇas, Āgamas and Bhārata. You know the past, present and future.

## \|\| 24.19-21 \|\|

*kaṣṭe 'smin duḥkhabahule niḥsāre bhavasāgare \|*  
*rāgagrāhākule raudre viṣayodakasaṃplave \|\| 19 \|\|*

*indriyāvartakalile dṛṣṭormiśatasaṃkule \|*  
*mohapaṅkāvile durge lobhagambhīradustare \|\| 20 \|\|*

*nimajjaj jagad ālokya nirālambam acetanam \|*  
*pṛcchāmas tvāṃ mahābhāgaṃ brūhi no munisattama \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. O excellent sage, tell us. We ask you the highly pleased soul, the following things on seeing the universe submerging in the ocean of worldly existence without any support and (miserably) unconscious (of the same). This ocean of worldly existence is painful and utterly full of misery. It has no Teal substance. It is terrible with passions acting like crocodiles, the objects of sense-organs acting like flood waters, the sense-organs like a blended mass of whirlpool, the visible objects like hundreds of confused masses of waves, delusion making it turbid like mud. It is impassable, grave and difficult to be crossed due to covetousness.

## \|\| 24.22 \|\|

*śreyaḥ kim atra saṃsāre bhairave lomaharṣaṇe \|*  
*upadeśapradānena lokān uddhartum arhasi \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. What is it that is conducive to welfare in this terrible world that causes hairs to stand on end. It behoves you to uplift the worlds by offering advice.

## \|\| 24.23 \|\|

*durlabhaṃ paramaṃ kṣetraṃ vaktum arhasi mokṣadam \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ karmabhūmiṃ ca śrotum icchāmahe vayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. It behoves you to recount that rare and extremely great holy centre which bestows liberation, We wish to hear about the land of holy rites on this earth.

## \|\| 24.24-25 \|\|

*kṛtvā kila naraḥ samyak karma bhūmau yathoditam \|*  
*prāpnoti paramāṃ siddhiṃ narakaṃ ca vikarmataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*mokṣakṣetre tathā mokṣaṃ prāpnoti puruṣaḥ sudhīḥ \|*  
*tasmād brūhi mahāprājña yat pṛṣṭo 'si dvijottama \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. It is only by perfectly performing the holy rites on this earth in the manner they have been laid down that a man attains the greatest perfection. By repugnant activities he falls into hell. The intelligent man attains absolution in the holy centre of salvation. Hence, O highly intelligent one, recount what you have been asked by the excellent brahmins.

## \|\| 24.26 \|\|

*śrutvā tu vacanaṃ teṣāṃ munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*vyāsaḥ provāca bhagavān bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyavit \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On hearing the words of those sages of purified souls the intelligent Vyāsa, conversant with the past and future said:

## \|\| 24.27-30 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*śṛṇudhvaṃ munayaḥ sarve vakṣyāmi yadi pṛcchatha \|*  
*yaḥ saṃvādo 'bhavat pūrvam ṛṣīṇāṃ brahmaṇā saha \|\| 27 \|\|*

*merupṛṣṭhe tu vistīrṇe nānāratnavibhūṣite \|*  
*nānādrumalatākīrṇe nānāpuṣpopaśobhite \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nānāpakṣirute ramye nānāprasavanākule \|*  
*nānāsattvasamākīrṇe nānāścaryasamanvite \|\| 29 \|\|*

*nānāvarṇaśilākīrṇe nānādhātuvibhūṣite \|*  
*nānāmunijanākīrṇe nānāśramasamanvite \|\| 30 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

27-30. Listen O sages. I shall mention as you ask, the conversation that formerly took place between the sages and Brahmā on the summit of Meru that is spacious and bedecked with variety of jewels. It abounds in many trees and creepers rendered splendid by diverse kinds of flowers. There the atmosphere is full of chirping sounds of various birds. It is literally scattered with animals with a confusing mass of their offsprings. Many wonderful and mysterious things are present there. Rocks and pebbles of different colour lie scattered embellished with, minerals and metals of all kinds. It contains several hermitages thronged with sages.

## \|\| 24.31-33 \|\|

*tatrāsīnaṃ jagannāthaṃ jagadyoniṃ caturmukham \|*  
*jagatpatiṃ jagadvandyaṃ jagadādhāram īśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

*devadānavagandharvair yakṣavidyādharoragaiḥ \|*  
*munisiddhāpsarobhiś ca vṛtam anyair divālayaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kecit stuvanti taṃ devaṃ kecid gāyanti cāgrataḥ \|*  
*kecid vādyāni vādyante kecin nṛtyanti cāpare \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. The four-faced lord of the universe was seated there. He is the source of origin of the universe. Being the lord and support of worlds, he is worthy of being saluted by all. He was then surrounded by Devas, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, serpents, sages, Siddhas, Apsarās and other heaven-dwellers. Some of them were eulogising him. Some were playing on musical instruments and singing songs in his praise. Others were dancing.

## \|\| 24.34-35 \|\|

*evaṃ pramudite kāle sarvabhūtasamāgame \|*  
*nānākusumagandhāḍhye dakṣiṇānilasevite \|\| 34 \|\|*

*bhṛgvādyās taṃ tadā devaṃ praṇipatya pitāmaham \|*  
*imam artham ṛṣivarāḥ papracchuḥ pitaraṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Thus, when the time was joyous and the living beings had gathered together, when the gentle southern breeze served them wafting the sweet odour from different kinds of flowers, Bhṛgu and other sages bowed to lord Brahmā. O brahmins, those excellent sages asked the father this very same topic.

## \|\| 24.36-37 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ:*  
*bhagavañ śrotum icchāmaḥ karmabhūmiṃ mahītale \|*  
*vaktum arhasi deveśa mokṣakṣetraṃ ca durlabham \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*teṣāṃ vacanam ākarṇya prāha brahmā sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*papracchus te yathā praśnaṃ tat sarvaṃ munisattamāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

The sages said:

36-37. “O lord, we wish to hear about the land of holy rites on the surface of the earth. O lord of Devas, it behoves you to recount the most inaccessible centre of absolution”

## Chapter 25 - Bhārata Subcontinent

## \|\| 25.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca:*  
*śṛṇudhvaṃ munayaḥ sarve yad vo vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam \|*  
*purāṇaṃ vedasaṃbaddhaṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ śubham \|\| 1 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

1\. O sages, you listen to what 1 am going to say now. It is a splendid ancient traditional account connected with the Vedas. It grants worldly pleasures and salvation.

## \|\| 25.2 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ bhārataṃ varṣaṃ karmabhūmir udāhṛtā \|*  
*karmaṇaḥ phalabhūmiś ca svargaṃ ca narakaṃ tathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Bhārata sub-continent is the land of holy rites in the whole of the earth. Heaven and hell are the lands for reaping the fruit of those holy rites.

## \|\| 25.3 \|\|

*tasmin varṣe naraḥ pāpaṃ kṛtvā dharmaṃ ca bho dvijāḥ \|*  
*avaśyaṃ phalam āpnoti aśubhasya śubhasya ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O brahmins, by committing sins or performing holy rites in that subcontinent a man necessarily attains the fruit thereof whether auspicious or inauspicious.

## \|\| 25.4 \|\|

*brāhmaṇādyāḥ svakaṃ karma kṛtvā samyak susaṃyatāḥ \|*  
*prāpnuvanti parāṃ siddhiṃ tasmin varṣe na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There is no doubt that by performing their ordained duties in that sub-continent, the brahmins and others of perfect self-control attain the highest success.

## \|\| 25.5 \|\|

*dharmaṃ cārthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*prāpnoti puruṣaḥ sarvaṃ tasmin varṣe susaṃyataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. O excellent brahmins, in that Varṣa, a person of self-control attains everything viz. virtue, wealth, love and liberation.

## \|\| 25.6 \|\|

*indrādyāś ca surāḥ sarve tasmin varṣe dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā suśobhanaṃ karma devatvaṃ pratipedire \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O excellent brahmins, Indra and other Devas have attained the status of a deity after performing splendid holy rites in that sub-continent.

## \|\| 25.7 \|\|

*anye 'pi lebhire mokṣaṃ puruṣāḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ \|*  
*tasmin varṣe budhāḥ śāntā vītarāgā vimatsarāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Other men too had attained salvation in that Varṣa. They had control over their organs. They were devoid of passion and indecent rivalry.

## \|\| 25.8 \|\|

*ye cāpi svarge tiṣṭhanti vimānena gatajvarāḥ \|*  
*te 'pi kṛtvā śubhaṃ karma tasmin varṣe divaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Those persons who are devoid of ailments and who stay in heaven with aerial chariots had previously performed splendid holy rites in that land of Bharata and had attained heaven thereby.

## \|\| 25.9 \|\|

*nivāsaṃ bhārate varṣa ākāṅkṣanti sadā surāḥ \|*  
*svargāpavargaphalade tat paśyāmaḥ kadā vayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Devas do always wish for a residence in Bhārata that yields the benefit of heavenly pleasures and liberation. They often spoke “O when shall we visit Bharata”.

## \|\| 25.10-13 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ:*  
*yad etad bhavatā proktaṃ karma nānyatra puṇyadam \|*  
*pāpāya vā suraśreṣṭha varjayitvā ca bhāratam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tataḥ svargaś ca mokṣaś ca madhyamaṃ tac ca gamyate \|*  
*na khalv anyatra martyānāṃ bhūmau karma vidhīyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tasmād vistarato brahmann asmākaṃ bhārataṃ vada \|*  
*yadi te 'sti dayāsmāsu yathāvasthitir eva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tasmād varṣam idaṃ nātha ye vāsmin varṣaparvatāḥ \|*  
*bhedāś ca tasya varṣasya brūhi sarvān aśeṣataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. O most excellent one among Devas, it has just been stated by you that except in Bhārata, rites holy or unholy are not conducive to meritorious or sinful results. But it seems likely that holy rites are not enjoined on men elsewhere. Hence, O Brahmā, recount Bhārata to us in detail, if you are kind to us. O lord, mention everything, how this sub-continent is situated. What are the continent mountains here? What are its divisions.

## \|\| 25.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca:*  
*śṛṇudhvaṃ bhārataṃ varṣaṃ navabhedena bho dvijāḥ \|*  
*samudrāntaritā jñeyās te samāś ca parasparam \|\| 14 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

14\. Listen, O brahmins, the Bhārata sub-continent has nine sub-divisions which are separated by oceans. They are equal to one another.

## \|\| 25.15-16 \|\|

*indradvīpaḥ kaśeruś ca tāmravarṇo gabhastimān \|*  
*nāgadvīpas tathā saumyo gāndharvo vāruṇas tathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ayaṃ tu navamas teṣāṃ dvīpaḥ sāgarasaṃvṛtaḥ \|*  
*yojanānāṃ sahasraṃ vai dvīpo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇottaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. They are Indradvīpa, Kaseru, Tāmravarṇa (? Tāmraparṇa), Gabhastimān, Nāgadvīpa, Saumya, Gandharva and Varuṇa. Bhārata surrounded by the ocean is the ninth among them. The island extends from south to north and is one thousand Yojanas long.

## \|\| 25.17 \|\|

*pūrve kirātā yasyāsan paścime yavanās tathā \|*  
*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāś cānte sthitā dvijāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the east of it, the Kirātas stay. The Yavanas stay in the west. O brahmins, the Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras stay in the middle.

## \|\| 25.18-20 \|\|

*ijyāyuddhavaṇijyādyaiḥ karmabhiḥ kṛtapāvanāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ saṃvyavahāraś ca ebhiḥ karmabhir iṣyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*svargāpavargahetuś ca puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ ca vai tathā \|*  
*mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śuktimān ṛkṣaparvataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vindhyaś ca pāriyātraś ca saptaivātra kulācalāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ sahasraśaś cānye bhūdharā ye samīpagāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. They are sanctified by holy rites and worldly pursuits as sacrifice, warfare, trading. Their general behaviour is intelligible through their activities, which cause heavenly pleasures and liberation. They incur merit and sin thereby.

There are seven Kula mountains viz., Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śūktimān, Ṛkṣa, Vindhya and Pāriyātra. There are thousauds of other mountains nearby.

## \|\| 25.21-24 \|\|

*vistārocchrayiṇo ramyā vipulāś citrasānavaḥ \|*  
*kolāhalaḥ sa vaibhrājo mandaro dardalācalaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vātaṃdhayo vaidyutaś ca mainākaḥ surasas tathā \|*  
*tuṅgaprastho nāgagirir godhanaḥ pāṇḍarācalaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*puṣpagirir vaijayanto raivato 'rbuda eva ca \|*  
*ṛṣyamūkaḥ sa gomanthaḥ kṛtaśailaḥ kṛtācalaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śrīpārvataś cakoraś ca śataśo 'nye ca parvatāḥ \|*  
*tair vimiśrā janapadā mlecchādyāś caiva bhāgaśaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*
