*ghātanīyau niyuddhāya raṅgadvāram upāgatau \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Considering their super-human activity that could not at all have been imagined (in persons of their age) Sandīpani thought that the moon and the sun had come to him.

## \|\| 86.23 \|\|

*tam ājñāpyātha dṛṣṭvā ca mañcān sarvān upāhṛtān \|*  
*āsannamaraṇaḥ kaṃsaḥ sūryodayam udaikṣata \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The moment they were uttered, (the two brothers) learned the Mantras of all miraculous missiles. They said—“What monetary gift should be paid as the preceptor’s fees? That may be mentioned.”

## \|\| 86.24 \|\|

*tataḥ samastamañceṣu nāgaraḥ sa tadā janaḥ \|*  
*rājamañceṣu cārūḍhāḥ saha bhṛtyair mahībhṛtaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Observing their ability to act beyond the pale of sense-organs the highly intelligent preceptor requested (the resuscitation) of his son who was dead in the holy centre of Prabhāsa on the shore of the briny sea.

## \|\| 86.25 \|\|

*mallaprāśnikavargaś ca raṅgamadhye samīpagaḥ \|*  
*kṛtaḥ kaṃsena kaṃso 'pi tuṅgamañce vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Equipped with their arms they went to the briny ocean. They said to the sea—“May the son of our preceptor be restored”.

## \|\| 86.26-27 \|\|

*antaḥpurāṇāṃ mañcāś ca yathānye parikalpitāḥ \|*  
*anye ca vāramukhyānām anye nagarayoṣitām \|\| 26 \|\|*

*nandagopādayo gopā mañceṣv anyeṣv avasthitāḥ \|*  
*akrūravasudevau ca mañcaprānte vyavasthitau \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. With palms joined in reverence and having the vessel of Arghya with him, the great ocean said—“The son of Sandīpani has not been abducted by me. An asura named Pañcajana, assumed the form of a conch and abducted the child. O slayer of Asuras, he is staying in my waters.”

## \|\| 86.28 \|\|

*nagarīyoṣitāṃ madhye devakī putragardhinī \|*  
*antakāle 'pi putrasya drakṣyāmīti mukhaṃ sthitā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On being told thus, Kṛṣṇa went inside the water, killed Pañcajana and took the excellent conch originating from his bones.

## \|\| 86.29-32 \|\|

*vādyamāneṣu tūryeṣu cāṇūre cātivalgati \|*  
*hāhākārapare loka āsphoṭayati muṣṭike \|\| 29 \|\|*

*hatvā kuvalayāpīḍaṃ hastyārohapracoditam \|*  
*madāsṛganuliptāṅgau gajadantavarāyudhau \|\| 30 \|\|*

*mṛgamadhye yathā siṃhau garvalīlāvalokinau \|*  
*praviṣṭau sumahāraṅgaṃ baladevajanārdanau \|\| 31 \|\|*

*hāhākāro mahāñ jajñe sarvaraṅgeṣv anantaram \|*  
*kṛṣṇo 'yaṃ balabhadro 'yam iti lokasya vismayāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. The conch Pāñcajanya’s sound reduced the strength of asuras, increased the refulgence of Devas and destroyed evil. Kṛṣṇa and the powerful Balarāma blew the conch Pāñcajanya and went to the city of Yama. There they conquered Yama, son of Vivasvat and regained the boy who was in the tortures of hell, who now got back a body as before. Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, the most excellent among the strong ones, gave the boy to his father. Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa returned to Mathurā protected by Ugrasena. They delighted men and women there.

## Chapter 87 - The Onslaught of Jarāsandha

## \|\| 87.1-2 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*rājamārge tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sānulepanabhājanām \|*  
*dadarśa kubjām āyāntīṃ navayauvanagocarām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tām āha lalitaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kasyedam anulepanam \|*  
*bhavatyā nīyate satyaṃ vadendīvaralocane \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

1-2. Kaṃsa of great strength had married the two daughters of Jarāsandha named Asti and Prāpti. O brahmins, Jarāsandha the powerful king of Magadha came there in great fury surrounded by a great army. It was to kill Kṛṣṇa together with the Yādavas that he came there, for Kṛṣṇa had killed the husband of his two daughters.

## \|\| 87.3 \|\|

*sakāmenaiva sā proktā sānurāgā hariṃ prati \|*  
*prāha sā lalitaṃ kubjā dadarśa ca balāt tataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The lord of Magadha attacked the vicinity of Mathurā. He was accompanied by twenty-three Akṣauhiṇīs of the army.

## \|\| 87.4 \|\|

*kubjovāca:*  
*kānta kasmān na jānāsi kaṃsenāpi niyojitā \|*  
*naikavakreti vikhyātām anulepanakarmaṇi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Surrounded by only a limited number of soldiers, the powerful Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa came out of their city and fought with the strong soldiers.

## \|\| 87.5 \|\|

*nānyapiṣṭaṃ hi kaṃsasya prītaye hy anulepanam \|*  
*bhavaty aham atīvāsya prasādadhanabhājanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thereafter, O excellent sages, Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa of great strength thought of taking up their ancient weapons.

## \|\| 87.6-8 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca:*  
*sugandham etad rājārhaṃ ruciraṃ rucirānane \|*  
*āvayor gātrasadṛśaṃ dīyatām anulepanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*śrutvā tam āha sā kṛṣṇaṃ gṛhyatām iti sādaram \|*  
*anulepaṃ ca pradadau gātrayogyam athobhayoḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhakticchedānuliptāṅgau tatas tau puruṣarṣabhau \|*  
*sendracāpau virājantau sitakṛṣṇāv ivāmbudau \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. The discus, the śārṅga bow, two quivers with inexhaustible supply of arrows and the iron club named Kaumodaki—all these came from the firmament to those heroes.

The ploughshare came into the hand of Balarāma from the sky. O brahmins, it resembled the Saṃvarta fire. So also the Musala (iron-club) called Sunanda came over to them.

In the battle, the heroic lads Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa defeated the king of Magadha together with his army.

## \|\| 87.9 \|\|

*tatas tāṃ cibuke śaurir ullāpanavidhānavit \|*  
*ullāpya tolayām āsa dvyaṅgulenāgrapāṇinā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O excellent brahmins, although Jarāsandha of evil design was conquered, Kṛṣṇa did not consider him defeated because he returned alive.

## \|\| 87.10 \|\|

*cakarṣa padbhyāṃ ca tadā ṛjutvaṃ keśavo 'nayat \|*  
*tataḥ sā ṛjutāṃ prāptā yoṣitām abhavad varā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O excellent brahmins, Jarāsandha came again accompanied by his huge army. He was conquered by Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa. He fled from the battlefield.

## \|\| 87.11 \|\|

*vilāsalalitaṃ prāha premagarbhabharālasam \|*  
*vastre pragṛhya govindaṃ vraja gehaṃ mameti vai \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus, the arrogant king of Magadha fought eighteen battles with the descendants of Yadu led by Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 87.12 \|\|

*āyāsye bhavatīgeham iti tāṃ prāha keśavaḥ \|*  
*visasarja jahāsoccai rāmasyālokya cānanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Although Jarāsandha had more armies he was defeated by the heroes of Yadu clan who had only a small army. He was defeated in all battles and he ñed on all occasions.

## \|\| 87.13 \|\|

*bhakticchedānuliptāṅgau nīlapītāmbarāv ubhau \|*  
*dhanuḥśālāṃ tato yātau citramālyopaśobhitau \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The fact that the army of Yādavas won all times indicates the greatness of discus-bearing Viṣṇu (i.e. Kṛṣṇa)

## \|\| 87.14 \|\|

*adhyāsya ca dhanūratnaṃ tābhyāṃ pṛṣṭais tu rakṣibhiḥ \|*  
*ākhyātaṃ sahasā kṛṣṇo gṛhītvāpūrayad dhanuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. It is a mere sport on the part of the lord of universe to discharge many forms of weapons on the enemies because the lord had human attributes and activities.

## \|\| 87.15 \|\|

*tataḥ pūrayatā tena bhajyamānaṃ balād dhanuḥ \|*  
*cakārātimahāśabdaṃ mathurā tena pūritā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In fact with his mere mental thought he can create and annihilate the universe. What detailed attempt need he make in destroying the enemy’s sides?

## \|\| 87.16 \|\|

*anuyuktau tatas tau ca bhagne dhanuṣi rakṣibhiḥ \|*  
*rakṣisainyaṃ nikṛtyobhau niṣkrāntau kārmukālayāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Still the lord follows the activities of human beings. Allying himself with the strong persons he fights with the weaker ones.

## \|\| 87.17-18 \|\|

*akrūrāgamavṛttāntam upalabhya tathā dhanuḥ \|*  
*bhagnaṃ śrutvātha kaṃso 'pi prāha cāṇūramuṣṭikau \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kaṃsa uvāca:*  
*gopāladārakau prāptau bhavadbhyāṃ tau mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*mallayuddhena hantavyau mama prāṇaharau hi tau \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. He uses the four strategic expedients such as peaceful overtures, gifts, threats or creating dissention in enemies ranks and the actual striking. In some places he resorts to fleeing. The sport of the lord of universe functions according to his will. He imitates the activities of embodied human beings.

## Chapter 88 - Mucukunda’s Prayer

## \|\| 88.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*rājamārge tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sānulepanabhājanām \|*  
*dadarśa kubjām āyāntīṃ navayauvanagocarām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

1\. O brahmins, Śyāla called a brahmin of the cowherds colony (named) Gārgya by the (ignoble remark) Śaṇḍha (impotent) in the presence of Yādavas and all the Yādavas laughed at it.

## \|\| 88.2 \|\|

*tām āha lalitaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kasyedam anulepanam \|*  
*bhavatyā nīyate satyaṃ vadendīvaralocane \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Thereupon, the infuriated brahmin went to Southern territory and performed a penance. He was desirous of a son who would be a terror to the Yādavas.

## \|\| 88.3 \|\|

*sakāmenaiva sā proktā sānurāgā hariṃ prati \|*  
*prāha sā lalitaṃ kubjā dadarśa ca balāt tataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Propitiating lord Śiva he ate powdered iron. The lord was pleased with him in the twelfth year and he granted him a boon.

## \|\| 88.4 \|\|

*kubjovāca:*  
*kānta kasmān na jānāsi kaṃsenāpi niyojitā \|*  
*naikavakreti vikhyātām anulepanakarmaṇi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Yavaneśa (a Greek King) who had no son honoured him. As a result of sexual intercourse with his wife a son of fiery splendour was born to him.

## \|\| 88.5 \|\|

*nānyapiṣṭaṃ hi kaṃsasya prītaye hy anulepanam \|*  
*bhavaty aham atīvāsya prasādadhanabhājanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He was named Kālayavana. The Greek king crowned the boy who had a chest as hard as the adamantine tip and went to the forest.

## \|\| 88.6 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca:*  
*sugandham etad rājārhaṃ ruciraṃ rucirānane \|*  
*āvayor gātrasadṛśaṃ dīyatām anulepanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Proud and arrogant by virtue of his prowess, he asked about the powerful kings on the Earth. Nārada told him about the Yādavas.

## \|\| 88.7 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*śrutvā tam āha sā kṛṣṇaṃ gṛhyatām iti sādaram \|*  
*anulepaṃ ca pradadau gātrayogyam athobhayoḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He was surrounded by crores and thousands of crores of Mlecchas (alien tribes) who were richly equipped with elephants, horses and chariots. He made an elaborate attempt thus.

## \|\| 88.8 \|\|

*bhakticchedānuliptāṅgau tatas tau puruṣarṣabhau \|*  
*sendracāpau virājantau sitakṛṣṇāv ivāmbudau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O sages, he was ceaselessly thinking of the Yādavas everyday. He became very furious with them. He marched against the city of Mathurā.

## \|\| 88.9-12 \|\|

*tatas tāṃ cibuke śaurir ullāpanavidhānavit \|*  
*ullāpya tolayām āsa dvyaṅgulenāgrapāṇinā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*cakarṣa padbhyāṃ ca tadā ṛjutvaṃ keśavo 'nayat \|*  
*tataḥ sā ṛjutāṃ prāptā yoṣitām abhavad varā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vilāsalalitaṃ prāha premagarbhabharālasam \|*  
*vastre pragṛhya govindaṃ vraja gehaṃ mameti vai \|\| 11 \|\|*

*āyāsye bhavatīgeham iti tāṃ prāha keśavaḥ \|*  
*visasarja jahāsoccai rāmasyālokya cānanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

9-12. Kṛṣṇa thought thus:—“On observing the Yādava army destroyed by Kālayavana, the king of Magadha will strike at us. The powerful Kālayavana will destroy the exhausted army of the king of Magadha. Thus two types of calamity are likely to befall us. Hence I shall make a very invincible fort for my clan. Even ladies can fight from within it. What then about the leading Vṛṣṇis? May not the wicked enemies harm the Yādavas much when I am inebriate, erring, sleeping or out of the territory.”

## \|\| 88.13 \|\|

*bhakticchedānuliptāṅgau nīlapītāmbarāv ubhau \|*  
*dhanuḥśālāṃ tato yātau citramālyopaśobhitau \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After thinking thus Kṛṣṇa begged of the great ocean a piece twelve Yojana. He created the city of Dvārakā there.

## \|\| 88.14 \|\|

*adhyāsya ca dhanūratnaṃ tābhyāṃ pṛṣṭais tu rakṣibhiḥ \|*  
*ākhyātaṃ sahasā kṛṣṇo gṛhītvāpūrayad dhanuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. It had great parks and outer walls. It was beautified by hundreds of lakes. It had hundreds of thick ramparts. It resembled Indra’s city Amarāvatī.

## \|\| 88.15 \|\|

*tataḥ pūrayatā tena bhajyamānaṃ balād dhanuḥ \|*  
*cakārātimahāśabdaṃ mathurā tena pūritā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Lord Kṛṣṇa brought the people of Mathurā there. When Kālayavana was expected he alone went to Mathurā.

## \|\| 88.16 \|\|

*anuyuktau tatas tau ca bhagne dhanuṣi rakṣibhiḥ \|*  
*rakṣisainyaṃ nikṛtyobhau niṣkrāntau kārmukālayāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When the army (of Kālayavana) encamped outside Mathurā, he came out without any weapon and the Yavana saw him.

## \|\| 88.17-18 \|\|

*akrūrāgamavṛttāntam upalabhya tathā dhanuḥ \|*  
*bhagnaṃ śrutvātha kaṃso 'pi prāha cāṇūramuṣṭikau \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kaṃsa uvāca:*  
*gopāladārakau prāptau bhavadbhyāṃ tau mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*mallayuddhena hantavyau mama prāṇaharau hi tau \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Knowing that he was Vāsudeva, the king too with his arms alone for weapons, followed the lord who is not attained even by the minds of great Yogins. Followed by him Kṛṣṇa entered a cave where king Mucukunda was lying asleep.

## \|\| 88.19 \|\|

*niyuddhe tadvināśena bhavadbhyāṃ toṣito hy aham \|*  
*dāsyāmy abhimatān kāmān nānyathaitan mahābalau \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Yavana also entered the cave. He saw a man lying on a bed. Thinking him to be Kṛṣṇa, the wicked Yavana kicked him with his foot.

## \|\| 88.20 \|\|

*nyāyato 'nyāyato vāpi bhavadbhyāṃ tau mamāhitau \|*  
*hantavyau tadvadhād rājyaṃ sāmānyaṃ vo bhaviṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The moment the Yavana was seen by him he was consumed by the fire of anger. O sages, he was instantaneously reduced to ashes.

## \|\| 88.21 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*ity ādiśya sa tau mallau tataś cāhūya hastipam \|*  
*provācoccais tvayā mattaḥ samājadvāri kuñjaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That king had taken part in the battle between Devas and Asuras and defeated Asuras. He had to remain for many nights without sleep and so was distressed. He requested Suras for the boon of slumber.

## \|\| 88.22 \|\|

*sthāpyaḥ kuvalayāpīḍas tena tau gopadārakau \|*  
*ghātanīyau niyuddhāya raṅgadvāram upāgatau \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He was also informed by Devas thus—“He who wakes you up when you are asleep will soon be reduced to ashes by the fire issuing from your body.

## \|\| 88.23 \|\|

*tam ājñāpyātha dṛṣṭvā ca mañcān sarvān upāhṛtān \|*  
*āsannamaraṇaḥ kaṃsaḥ sūryodayam udaikṣata \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After reducing that sinner he looked at Kṛṣṇa and said—“Who are you?” Kṛṣṇa said: “I am born of the lunar race.

## \|\| 88.24-25 \|\|

*tataḥ samastamañceṣu nāgaraḥ sa tadā janaḥ \|*  
*rājamañceṣu cārūḍhāḥ saha bhṛtyair mahībhṛtaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*mallaprāśnikavargaś ca raṅgamadhye samīpagaḥ \|*  
*kṛtaḥ kaṃsena kaṃso 'pi tuṅgamañce vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. I am the son of Vasudeva, the scion of the family of Yadu”.

On hearing it Mucukunda remembered the words of the elderly Gārgya. After recollecting everything he bowed down to Kṛṣṇa, the lord of all identical with everyone. He said—“You are the greatest īśvara. You are born of Viṣṇu’s part.

## \|\| 88.26 \|\|

*antaḥpurāṇāṃ mañcāś ca yathānye parikalpitāḥ \|*  
*anye ca vāramukhyānām anye nagarayoṣitām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Formerly, this was mentioned by Gārgya—Hari will take birth in the line of Yadu towards the end of Dvāpara Yuga in the twenty-eighth cycle of four Yugas.

## \|\| 88.27-30 \|\|

*nandagopādayo gopā mañceṣv anyeṣv avasthitāḥ \|*  
*akrūravasudevau ca mañcaprānte vyavasthitau \|\| 27 \|\|*

*nagarīyoṣitāṃ madhye devakī putragardhinī \|*  
*antakāle 'pi putrasya drakṣyāmīti mukhaṃ sthitā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vādyamāneṣu tūryeṣu cāṇūre cātivalgati \|*  
*hāhākārapare loka āsphoṭayati muṣṭike \|\| 29 \|\|*

*hatvā kuvalayāpīḍaṃ hastyārohapracoditam \|*  
*madāsṛganuliptāṅgau gajadantavarāyudhau \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. Therefore, there is no doubt at all. You are the one come to me. You are the one that render help to all men, I am unable to endure your great splendour. He uttered words unto him so bold and resonant as the rumbling sound of the rain-bearing cloud, to him who was petted and fondled by you. However, in the great battle between Devas and Asuras the heroic Devas and Asuras were incompetent to endure your great refulgence. I too am unable to bear that refulgence. You are the greatest refuge to the creature that has fallen in the ocean of worldly existence. You are the sole dispeller of agony of those who resort to you. Be pleased. Remove my inauspiciousness.

## \|\| 88.31 \|\|

*mṛgamadhye yathā siṃhau garvalīlāvalokinau \|*  
*praviṣṭau sumahāraṅgaṃ baladevajanārdanau \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. You are everything viz—oceans, mountains, rivers, forests, Earth, sky, wind, water, fire, you are the highest being.

## \|\| 88.32-35 \|\|

*hāhākāro mahāñ jajñe sarvaraṅgeṣv anantaram \|*  
*kṛṣṇo 'yaṃ balabhadro 'yam iti lokasya vismayāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

*so 'yaṃ yena hatā ghorā pūtanā sā niśācarī \|*  
*prakṣiptaṃ śakaṭaṃ yena bhagnau ca yamalārjunau \|\| 33 \|\|*

*so 'yaṃ yaḥ kāliyaṃ nāgaṃ nanartāruhya bālakaḥ \|*  
*dhṛto govardhano yena saptarātraṃ mahāgiriḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ariṣṭo dhenukaḥ keśī līlayaiva mahātmanā \|*  
*hato yena ca durvṛtto dṛśyate so 'yam acyutaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. You are the one devoid of sound etc., the unageing one devoid of birth and destruction. All beings attain their series of births from you who pervade everything. The immortal beings, Pitṛs (Manes) Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Rākṣasas, Siddhas, Apsarās—attain their births from you—men, animals, birds, reptiles, deer, trees, and the time-scale divided into past, present and future—everything mobile and immobile, all those things with or without forms, those which are gross and subtle—O creator of the universe, you alone are all those things; there is nothing without you.

## \|\| 88.36 \|\|

*ayaṃ cāsya mahābāhur baladevo 'grajo 'grataḥ \|*  
*prayāti līlayā yoṣin- manonayananandanaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O lord, no peace or happiness was attained by me anywhere; by me who wandered amidst the cycles of worldly existence and who had been attacked by the three forms of scorching agonies.

## \|\| 88.37 \|\|

*ayaṃ sa kathyate prājñaiḥ purāṇārthāvalokibhiḥ \|*  
*gopālo yādavaṃ vaṃśaṃ magnam abhyuddhariṣyati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O lord, miseries alone were taken up by me as pleasures, like the mirages that are understood as water-reservoirs. They were conducive to my agony alone.

## \|\| 88.38-39 \|\|

*ayaṃ sa sarvabhūtasya viṣṇor akhilajanmanaḥ \|*  
*avatīrṇo mahīm aṃśo nūnaṃ bhāraharo bhuvaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ity evaṃ varṇite paurai rāme kṛṣṇe ca tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*uras tatāpa devakyāḥ snehasnutapayodharam \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Kingdom, Earth, army, treasury, allies, sons, wives, attendants, and the objects of senses beginning with sound—all these, O unchanging one, were taken by me to be the cause of happiness. O lord of Devas, in effect they were sources of distress, of a scorching nature.

## \|\| 88.40 \|\|

*mahotsavam ivālokya putrāv eva vilokayan \|*  
*yuveva vasudevo 'bhūd vihāyābhyāgatāṃ jarām \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. O lord, even Devas attaining the goal of the common world became desirous of help from me. Where is permanent happiness (available)?

## \|\| 88.41 \|\|

*vistāritākṣiyugalā rājāntaḥpurayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*nāgarastrīsamūhaś ca draṣṭuṃ na virarāma tau \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Without propitiating you, the basis and source of origin of all the worlds, by whom is permanent happiness attained?

## \|\| 88.42 \|\|

*striya ūcuḥ:*  
*sakhyaḥ paśyata kṛṣṇasya mukham apy ambujekṣaṇam \|*  
*gajayuddhakṛtāyāsa- svedāmbukaṇikāñcitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. People whose minds are deluded by your Māyā attain birth, death, old age etc. of a sinful nature. They see the King of the dead in the middle.

## \|\| 88.43-45 \|\|

*vikāsīva sarombhojam avaśyāyajalokṣitam \|*  
*paribhūtākṣaraṃ janma saphalaṃ kriyatāṃ dṛśaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*śrīvatsāṅkaṃ jagaddhāma bālasyaitad vilokyatām \|*  
*vipakṣakṣapaṇaṃ vakṣo bhujayugmaṃ ca bhāmini \|\| 44 \|\|*

*valgatā muṣṭikenaiva cāṇūreṇa tathā paraiḥ \|*  
*kriyate balabhadrasya hāsyam īṣad vilokyatām \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. Then those men are bound by means of hundreds of nooses in hells. They attain very terrible misery. This is your cosmic form. I am very much sensuous. I am deluded by your Māyā, O great lord, I wander amidst deep pits of ‘my-ness’.

I have sought refuge in you. You who have no other side (? a vast one), the primordial Īśa, than whom there is no other greater region. My mind is distressed due to exhaustion and agony of worldly existence. I am desirous of attaining the transformed (?) shelter, being disgusted with worldly affairs.”

## Chapter 89 - Balarāma returns to the cowherds’ colony

## \|\| 89.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*rājamārge tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sānulepanabhājanām \|*  
*dadarśa kubjām āyāntīṃ navayauvanagocarām \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

1\. Eulogised thus by that intelligent Mucukunda, the lord of all living beings, the lord who has no beginning or death spoke thus.

## \|\| 89.2 \|\|

*tām āha lalitaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kasyedam anulepanam \|*  
*bhavatyā nīyate satyaṃ vadendīvaralocane \|\| 2 \|\|*

Śrīkṛṣṇa said:

2\. O lord of men, go to divine worlds as desired by you. You will be strengthened by my grace and your prosperity and prowess will be unimpeded.

## \|\| 89.3 \|\|

*sakāmenaiva sā proktā sānurāgā hariṃ prati \|*  
*prāha sā lalitaṃ kubjā dadarśa ca balāt tataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After enjoying the great divine pleasures, you will be born in a great family. By my favour you will be able to remember your previous births. Thereafter, you will attain salvation.

## \|\| 89.4 \|\|

*kubjovāca:*  
*kānta kasmān na jānāsi kaṃsenāpi niyojitā \|*  
*naikavakreti vikhyātām anulepanakarmaṇi \|\| 4 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

4\. Thus blessed by the lord the king bowed to Acyuta; the lord of the worlds came out of the cave. Then he saw short-statured men.

## \|\| 89.5 \|\|

*nānyapiṣṭaṃ hi kaṃsasya prītaye hy anulepanam \|*  
*bhavaty aham atīvāsya prasādadhanabhājanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The king understood that the Kaliyuga had arrived. He went to the abode of Nara and Nārāyaṇa in order to perform penance (on the mountain) Gandhamādana.

## \|\| 89.6 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca:*  
*sugandham etad rājārhaṃ ruciraṃ rucirānane \|*  
*āvayor gātrasadṛśaṃ dīyatām anulepanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Slaying the enemy by means of a stratagem, Kṛṣṇa captured his army shining with horses, elephants and chariots after arriving at Mathurā.

## \|\| 89.7 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*śrutvā tam āha sā kṛṣṇaṃ gṛhyatām iti sādaram \|*  
*anulepaṃ ca pradadau gātrayogyam athobhayoḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After bringing it to Dvāravatī he offered it to Ugrasena. (Thereby) the army of the Yadus had no fear of the onslaught of enemies.

## \|\| 89.8 \|\|

*bhakticchedānuliptāṅgau tatas tau puruṣarṣabhau \|*  
*sendracāpau virājantau sitakṛṣṇāv ivāmbudau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O leading brahmins, having subdued all quarrels Baladeva became eager to see his kinsmen and so went to the cowherds’ colony of Nanda.

## \|\| 89.9 \|\|

*tatas tāṃ cibuke śaurir ullāpanavidhānavit \|*  
*ullāpya tolayām āsa dvyaṅgulenāgrapāṇinā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. As before, the conqueror of enemies spoke to the cowherds and cowherd-lasses with affection and respect.

## \|\| 89.10 \|\|

*cakarṣa padbhyāṃ ca tadā ṛjutvaṃ keśavo 'nayat \|*  
*tataḥ sā ṛjutāṃ prāptā yoṣitām abhavad varā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He was embraced by them. He embraced some of them. With some cowherds and cowherdesses he cracked jokes.

## \|\| 89.11 \|\|

*vilāsalalitaṃ prāha premagarbhabharālasam \|*  
*vastre pragṛhya govindaṃ vraja gehaṃ mameti vai \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The cowherds spoke many pleasing words to Balarāma. Some cowherdesses spoke joyously in their love and others spoke with malice.

## \|\| 89.12 \|\|

*āyāsye bhavatīgeham iti tāṃ prāha keśavaḥ \|*  
*visasarja jahāsoccai rāmasyālokya cānanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Other cowherdesses asked thus:—“Is Kṛṣṇa the lover of womenfolk of the city happy? Is he agitated by stirring emotions of love.

## \|\| 89.13 \|\|

*bhakticchedānuliptāṅgau nīlapītāmbarāv ubhau \|*  
*dhanuḥśālāṃ tato yātau citramālyopaśobhitau \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Does not Kṛṣṇa whose affection is momentary, deride our activities and increase the good fortune and pride of the ladies of Mathurā.

## \|\| 89.14 \|\|

*adhyāsya ca dhanūratnaṃ tābhyāṃ pṛṣṭais tu rakṣibhiḥ \|*  
*ākhyātaṃ sahasā kṛṣṇo gṛhītvāpūrayad dhanuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Does Kṛṣṇa ever remember our following him and singing along with him? Will he come here at least once to see his mother?

## \|\| 89.15 \|\|

*tataḥ pūrayatā tena bhajyamānaṃ balād dhanuḥ \|*  
*cakārātimahāśabdaṃ mathurā tena pūritā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Or, of what avail is this talk regarding him? May other stories be mentioned, for without us his (life) is possible and without (him) our (life) is possible.

## \|\| 89.16 \|\|

*anuyuktau tatas tau ca bhagne dhanuṣi rakṣibhiḥ \|*  
*rakṣisainyaṃ nikṛtyobhau niṣkrāntau kārmukālayāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Father, mother, brother, husband and kinsmen—who is not abandoned by us for his sake. (But) he had been ungrateful.

## \|\| 89.17 \|\|

*akrūrāgamavṛttāntam upalabhya tathā dhanuḥ \|*  
*bhagnaṃ śrutvātha kaṃso 'pi prāha cāṇūramuṣṭikau \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Still, does Kṛṣṇa ever (mention) anything about his coming here? Nectar-like words must be uttered by you.

## \|\| 89.18 \|\|

*kaṃsa uvāca:*  
*gopāladārakau prāptau bhavadbhyāṃ tau mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*mallayuddhena hantavyau mama prāṇaharau hi tau \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He appears to be devoid of Jove towards us because his mind is attached to the ladies of the city. It seems it will be difficult to see him.”

## \|\| 89.19 \|\|

*niyuddhe tadvināśena bhavadbhyāṃ toṣito hy aham \|*  
*dāsyāmy abhimatān kāmān nānyathaitan mahābalau \|\| 19 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

19\. He (Balarāma) was called (by the cowherd-lasses) by the words Kṛṣṇa, Dāmodara etc. The cowherd-lasses whose minds were attracted by Kṛṣṇa laughed in good tune.

## \|\| 89.20 \|\|

*nyāyato 'nyāyato vāpi bhavadbhyāṃ tau mamāhitau \|*  
*hantavyau tadvadhād rājyaṃ sāmānyaṃ vo bhaviṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The cowherd-lasses were consoled by Rāma through gentle and sweet messages of Kṛṣṇa couched in loving emotions and devoid of arrogance. The notes were as sweet as honey.

## \|\| 89.21 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*ity ādiśya sa tau mallau tataś cāhūya hastipam \|*  
*provācoccais tvayā mattaḥ samājadvāri kuñjaraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. As before Balarāma continued funny stories and jokes with the cowherds whose minds were attracted by Kṛṣṇa, the cowherds who were the residents of Vraja.

## Chapter 90 - Balarāma’s sport with Ploughshare

## \|\| 90.1-2 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*rājamārge tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sānulepanabhājanām \|*  
*dadarśa kubjām āyāntīṃ navayauvanagocarām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tām āha lalitaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kasyedam anulepanam \|*  
*bhavatyā nīyate satyaṃ vadendīvaralocane \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

1-2. The noble lord Balarāma was thus roaming about in the forest along with the cowherds. He was Śeṣa the supporter of the Earth, who had assumed the false guise of a human being. He had accomplished great tasks. It was for fulfilling a great task that he had taken up this incarnation. Hence, for the purpose of his enjoyment Varuṇa spoke to Vāruṇī (wine).

## \|\| 90.3 \|\|

*sakāmenaiva sā proktā sānurāgā hariṃ prati \|*  
*prāha sā lalitaṃ kubjā dadarśa ca balāt tataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Varuṇa said:

3\. O wine, you have always been liked by (Balarāma) of great prowess, O auspicious one, go now for his joy and enjoyment of pleasures.

## \|\| 90.4 \|\|

*kubjovāca:*  
*kānta kasmān na jānāsi kaṃsenāpi niyojitā \|*  
*naikavakreti vikhyātām anulepanakarmaṇi \|\| 4 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

4\. Thus advised by him Vāruṇī (wine) stationed herself in the hollow of a Kadamba tree growing on the banks of Yamunā in Vṛndāvana.

## \|\| 90.5 \|\|

*nānyapiṣṭaṃ hi kaṃsasya prītaye hy anulepanam \|*  
*bhavaty aham atīvāsya prasādadhanabhājanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Roaming about that spot Balarāma inhaled the intensive odour of wine. After smelling it he experienced the delight that he previously used to have in wine.

## \|\| 90.6 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca:*  
*sugandham etad rājārhaṃ ruciraṃ rucirānane \|*  
*āvayor gātrasadṛśaṃ dīyatām anulepanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O sages, thereafter, Balarāma saw a current of liquor suddenly falling from Kadamba. He derived great joy therefrom.

## \|\| 90.7 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*śrutvā tam āha sā kṛṣṇaṃ gṛhyatām iti sādaram \|*  
*anulepaṃ ca pradadau gātrayogyam athobhayoḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He drank it joyously in the company of cowherds and cowherdesses while experts in songs and instrumental music sang elegantly.

## \|\| 90.8 \|\|

*bhakticchedānuliptāṅgau tatas tau puruṣarṣabhau \|*  
*sendracāpau virājantau sitakṛṣṇāv ivāmbudau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Shining with the pearl-like drops of sweat due to excessive heat and fatigue he became agitated and said—“O Yamunā, come hither. I wish to take my bath”.

## \|\| 90.9 \|\|

*tatas tāṃ cibuke śaurir ullāpanavidhānavit \|*  
*ullāpya tolayām āsa dvyaṅgulenāgrapāṇinā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The river disregarded those words of inebriated person. She did not approach him. The infuriated Balarāma (thereupon) seized his ploughshare.

## \|\| 90.10 \|\|

*cakarṣa padbhyāṃ ca tadā ṛjutvaṃ keśavo 'nayat \|*  
*tataḥ sā ṛjutāṃ prāptā yoṣitām abhavad varā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Agitated due to inebriation he caught hold of her by the tip of his ploughshare—“O evil-minded one, won’t you come, won’t you come? Then go elsewhere as you please”.

## \|\| 90.11 \|\|

*vilāsalalitaṃ prāha premagarbhabharālasam \|*  
*vastre pragṛhya govindaṃ vraja gehaṃ mameti vai \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Dragged by him suddenly the river left her usual path and Hooded the forest where Balarāma was present.

## \|\| 90.12 \|\|

*āyāsye bhavatīgeham iti tāṃ prāha keśavaḥ \|*  
*visasarja jahāsoccai rāmasyālokya cānanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. She approached him in an embodied form. Due to fear her eyes were agitated. She said to him “O you having lionclub as your weapon, be pleased, leave me off”.

## \|\| 90.13 \|\|

*bhakticchedānuliptāṅgau nīlapītāmbarāv ubhau \|*  
*dhanuḥśālāṃ tato yātau citramālyopaśobhitau \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He said:—“If you disregard me in spite of my heroism and strength I shall split you into a thousand bits with the blows of my ploughshare”.

## \|\| 90.14 \|\|

*adhyāsya ca dhanūratnaṃ tābhyāṃ pṛṣṭais tu rakṣibhiḥ \|*  
*ākhyātaṃ sahasā kṛṣṇo gṛhītvāpūrayad dhanuḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

14\. When he said thus, he was propitated by the river. When the ground there was flooded, Balarāma released Yamunā.

## \|\| 90.15-16 \|\|

*tataḥ pūrayatā tena bhajyamānaṃ balād dhanuḥ \|*  
*cakārātimahāśabdaṃ mathurā tena pūritā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*anuyuktau tatas tau ca bhagne dhanuṣi rakṣibhiḥ \|*  
*rakṣisainyaṃ nikṛtyobhau niṣkrāntau kārmukālayāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Splendour came to him in the forest when he had his bath. Lakṣmī took with her a blue lotus as his ornament, an car-ring, a garland of never-fading lotus flowers sent by Varuṇa and two blue cloths having the lustre of the sea and gave these presents to him.

## \|\| 90.17 \|\|

*akrūrāgamavṛttāntam upalabhya tathā dhanuḥ \|*  
*bhagnaṃ śrutvātha kaṃso 'pi prāha cāṇūramuṣṭikau \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Having adorned himself with the blue lotus, embellishing himself with the beautiful ear-ring and clad in blue garments, the glorious one shone with splendour.

## \|\| 90.18 \|\|

*kaṃsa uvāca:*  
*gopāladārakau prāptau bhavadbhyāṃ tau mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*mallayuddhena hantavyau mama prāṇaharau hi tau \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus embellished, Rāma sported there in the cowherds’ colony. After two months he went to Dvārakā.

## \|\| 90.19 \|\|

*niyuddhe tadvināśena bhavadbhyāṃ toṣito hy aham \|*  
*dāsyāmy abhimatān kāmān nānyathaitan mahābalau \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Balarāma married Revatī the daughter of king Raivata. Two sons, Niśaṭha and Ulumuka were born of her.

## Chapter 91 - Return of Pradyumna

## \|\| 91.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*bhīṣmakaḥ kuṇḍine rājā vidarbhaviṣaye 'bhavat \|*  
*rukmiṇī tasya duhitā rukmī caiva suto dvijāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

1\. Bhīṣmaka was the king of Kuṇḍina in the realm of Vidarbha. His son was Rukmin and his daughter was Rukmiṇī.

## \|\| 91.2 \|\|

*rukmiṇīṃ cakame kṛṣṇaḥ sā ca taṃ cāruhāsinī \|*  
*na dadau yācate caināṃ rukmī dveṣeṇa cakriṇe \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Kṛṣṇa loved Rukmiṇī and the lady of beautiful smiles loved him in return. Due to hatred, Rukmin did not give her to the discus-bearing lord.

## \|\| 91.3 \|\|

*dadau sa śiśupālāya jarāsaṃdhapracoditaḥ \|*  
*bhīṣmako rukmiṇā sārdhaṃ rukmiṇīm uruvikramaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Urged by Jarāsandha and Rukmin together, Bhīṣmaka of great exploit gave Rukmiṇī to Śiśupāla.

## \|\| 91.4 \|\|

*vivāhārthaṃ tataḥ sarve jarāsaṃdhamukhā nṛpāḥ \|*  
*bhīṣmakasya puraṃ jagmuḥ śiśupālaś ca kuṇḍinam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then for the purpose of marriage the kings led by Jarāsandha, and Śiśupāla went to Kuṇḍina the city of Bhīṣmaka.

## \|\| 91.5 \|\|

*kṛṣṇo 'pi balabhadrādyair yadubhiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*prayayau kuṇḍinaṃ draṣṭuṃ vivāhaṃ caidyabhūpateḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Surrounded by Balarāma and other scions of the Yadu, Kṛṣṇa went to Kuṇḍina to witness the marriage of Śiśupāla, the king of Cedī.

## \|\| 91.6-12 \|\|

*śvobhāvini vivāhe tu tāṃ kanyāṃ hṛtavān hariḥ \|*  
*vipakṣabhāvam āsādya rāmādyeṣv eva bandhuṣu \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tataś ca pauṇḍrakaḥ śrīmān dantavaktro vidūrathaḥ \|*  
*śiśupālo jarāsaṃdhaḥ śālvādyāś ca mahībhṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kupitās te hariṃ hantuṃ cakrur udyogam uttamam \|*  
*nirjitāś ca samāgamya rāmādyair yadupuṃgavaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kuṇḍinaṃ na pravekṣyāmi ahatvā yudhi keśavam \|*  
*kṛtvā pratijñāṃ rukmī ca hantuṃ kṛṣṇam abhidrutaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*hatvā balaṃ sa nāgāśva- pattisyandanasaṃkulam \|*  
*nirjitaḥ pātitaś corvyāṃ līlayaiva sa cakriṇā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nirjitya rukmiṇaṃ samyag upayeme sa rukmiṇīm \|*  
*rākṣasena vidhānena saṃprāpto madhusūdanaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ jajñe ca pradyumno madanāṃśaḥ sa vīryavān \|*  
*jahāra śambaro yaṃ vai yo jaghāna ca śambaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

6-12. On the eve of marriage day Kṛṣṇa abducted that virgin even as Rāma and other kinsmen were opposed to it. Then the glorious Pauṇḍraka, Dantavaktra, Vidūratha, Śiśupāla, Jarāsandha, Śalva and other kings became infuriated. Allying themselves with Balarāma and other leading scions of the family of Yadu they made earnest attempts to kill Kṛṣṇa but they were defeated. Taking the vow—“Without killing Kṛṣṇa in the battle I shall not re-enter Kuṇḍina”, Rukmin rushed at Kṛṣṇa to kill him. After killing his army fully equipped with elephants, horses, foot-soldiers and chariots the discus-bearing lord playfully hurled him on to the ground.

After defeating Rukmin Kṛṣṇa married Rukmiṇī duly in accordance with the injunctions regarding Rākṣasa type of marriage. The valorous Pradyumna, apart incarnation of cupid, was born of her. Śambara kidnapped him but he killed Śambara.

## \|\| 91.13 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ:*  
*śambareṇa hṛto vīraḥ pradyumnaḥ sa kathaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*śambaraś ca mahāvīryaḥ pradyumnena kathaṃ hataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

The sages said:

13\. How was that heroic one kidnapped by Śambara and how was Śambara killed by him? O highly intelligent one, narrate this divine anecdote to me.

## \|\| 91.14 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*ṣaṣṭhe 'hni jātamātre tu pradyumnaṃ sūtikāgṛhāt \|*  
*mamaiṣa hanteti dvijā hṛtavān kālaśambaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

14\. On the sixth day after his birth, O brahmins, Kālaśambara kidnapped Pradyumna from the lying-in-chamber thinking—“O this one will be my killer”.

## \|\| 91.15 \|\|

*nītvā cikṣepa caivainaṃ grāho 'gre lavaṇārṇave \|*  
*kallolajanitāvarte sughore makarālaye \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Taking the boy with him he hurled him into the briny sea, infested with crocodiles, the awful abode of sparks that abounded in eddies and whirlpools generated by billows.

## \|\| 91.16 \|\|

*patitaṃ caiva tatraiko matsyo jagrāha bālakam \|*  
*na mamāra ca tasyāpi jaṭharānaladīpitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. As the boy fell down there a fish caught hold of him. Though burned by its gastric fire the boy did not die.

## \|\| 91.17 \|\|

*matsyabandhaiś ca matsyo 'sau matsyair anyaiḥ saha dvijāḥ \|*  
*ghātito 'suravaryāya śambarāya niveditaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O brahmins, this fish along with other fishes was caught by fishermen and offered to Śambara the most excellent one among the Asuras.

## \|\| 91.18 \|\|

*tasya māyāvatī nāma patnī sarvagṛheśvarī \|*  
*kārayām āsa sūdānām ādhipatyam aninditā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. His wife named Māyāvatī, the uncensured queen of his household, supervised over the work of cooks.

## \|\| 91.19 \|\|

*dārite matsyajaṭhare dadṛśe sātiśobhanam \|*  
*kumāraṃ manmathataror dagdhasya prathamāṅkuram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When the belly of the fish was ripped open she saw an excessively splendid boy who was the first shooting sprout of the tree of cupid that had been burned.

## \|\| 91.20 \|\|

*ko 'yaṃ katham ayaṃ matsya- jaṭhare samupāgataḥ \|*  
*ity evaṃ kautukāviṣṭāṃ tāṃ tanvīṃ prāha nāradaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “Who is this? How did he happen to come into the belly of the fish?”

Nārada spoke to her:—

## \|\| 91.21-22 \|\|

*nārada uvāca:*  
*ayaṃ samastajagatāṃ sṛṣṭisaṃhārakāriṇā \|*  
*śambareṇa hṛtaḥ kṛṣṇa- tanayaḥ sūtikāgṛhāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kṣiptaḥ samudre matsyena nigīrṇas te vaśaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*nararatnam idaṃ subhru viśrabdhā paripālaya \|\| 22 \|\|*

Nārada said:

21-22. This is the son of Kṛṣṇa abducted from the lying in-chamber by Śambara who is capable of creating and annihilating the worlds. He was cast off into the ocean, was swallowed by a fish and now he has come under your control. O lady of good eyebrows, look after this jewel of a man confidently.

## \|\| 91.23-24 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*nāradenaivam uktā sā pālayām āsa taṃ śiśum \|*  
*bālyād evātirāgeṇa rūpātiśayamohitā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sa yadā yauvanābhoga- bhūṣito 'bhūd dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*sābhilāṣā tadā sā tu babhūva gajagāminī \|\| 24 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

23-24. Informed thus by Nārada she looked after the boy. Ever since the boyhood of the child she was fascinated by his excelling handsome features and overwhelmed by excess of love. O excellent brahmins, when he was embellished by extensive youthful features, that lady of graceful elephantine gait, became very much attached to him.

## \|\| 91.25 \|\|

*māyāvatī dadau cāsmai māyā sarvā mahātmane \|*  
*pradyumnāyātmabhūtāya tannyastahṛdayekṣaṇā \|*  
*prasajjantīṃ tu tām āha sa kārṣṇiḥ kamalalocanaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Māyāvati taught all the Māyās (illusory tricks) to the noble Pradyumna who was befitting her and in whom she had fixed her heart and the eyes. The lotus-eyed son of Kṛṣṇa told her who was attached to him.

## \|\| 91.26-31 \|\|

*pradyumna uvāca:*  
*mātṛbhāvaṃ vihāyaiva kimarthaṃ vartase 'nyathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*sā cāsmai kathayām āsa na putras tvaṃ mameti vai \|*  
*tanayaṃ tvām ayaṃ viṣṇor hṛtavān kālaśambaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kṣiptaḥ samudre matsyasya saṃprāpto jaṭharān mayā \|*  
*sā tu roditi te mātā kāntādyāpy ativatsalā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*ity uktaḥ śambaraṃ yuddhe pradyumnaḥ sa samāhvayat \|*  
*krodhākulīkṛtamanā yuyudhe ca mahābalaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*hatvā sainyam aśeṣaṃ tu tasya daityasya mādhaviḥ \|*  
*sapta māyā vyatikramya māyāṃ saṃyuyuje 'ṣṭamīm \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tayā jaghāna taṃ daityaṃ māyayā kālaśambaram \|*  
*utpatya ca tayā sārdham ājagāma pituḥ puram \|\| 31 \|\|*

Pradyumna said:

26-31. Setting aside the emotions of a mother why do you behave like this in an entirely different manner?

## \|\| 91.32 \|\|

*antaḥpure ca patitaṃ māyāvatyā samanvitam \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭasaṃkalpā babhūvuḥ kṛṣṇayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*rukmiṇī cābravīt premṇā āsaktadṛṣṭir aninditā \|\| 32 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

She told him—“You are not my son. Kālaśambara kidnapped you, the son of Kṛṣṇa. You were cast off into the ocean. You were obtained by me from the belly of a fish. Your mother is crying now but your beloved is extremely fond of you”.

Vyāsa said:

Thus informed Pradyumna challenged Śambata for a fight. With his mind turned turbulent due to fury the powerful one fought. After killing the entire army of that asura, Pradyumna, son of Kṛṣṇa passed over seven Māyās and employed the eighth one too. With that Māyā he killed Śambara.

Then he returned to the city of his father accompanied by her.

32\. On seeing him present in the harem accompanied by Māyāvatī, Kṛṣṇa’s wives had delightful ideas. The uncensured lady Rukmiṇī said with her eyes fixed on him with affection.

## \|\| 91.33 \|\|

*rukmiṇy uvāca:*  
*dhanyāyāḥ khalv ayaṃ putro vartate navayauvane \|*  
*asmin vayasi putro me pradyumno yadi jīvati \|\| 33 \|\|*

Rukmiṇī said:

33\. This is the son of a fortunate lady. He is in the freshness of his youth. If my son Pradyumna were alive he would be of this age.

## \|\| 91.34 \|\|

*sabhāgyā jananī vatsa tvayā kāpi vibhūṣitā \|*  
*athavā yādṛśaḥ sneho mama yādṛg vapuś ca te \|*  
*harer apatyaṃ suvyaktaṃ bhavān vatsa bhaviṣyati \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. O my beloved child, your mother is fortunate whoever she be, she is embellished by you. Or, (considering from the way) my affection turns and from your physical features, it it clear that you are Kṛṣṇa’s son.

## \|\| 91.35 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*etasminn antare prāptaḥ saha kṛṣṇena nāradaḥ \|*  
*antaḥpuravarāṃ devīṃ rukmiṇīṃ prāha harṣitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

35\. In the meantime, Nārada came there along with Kṛṣṇa. Delighted he said to the gentle lady Rukmiṇī who was moving about in the harem:

## \|\| 91.36 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca:*  
*eṣa te tanayaḥ subhru hatvā śambaram āgataḥ \|*  
*hṛto yenābhavat pūrvaṃ putras te sūtikāgṛhāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

Śrīkṛṣṇa said:

36\. O lady of fine eyebrows, this is your son who has come here after killing Śambara by whom he had been abducted from your lying-in-chamber when he was but an infant boy.

## \|\| 91.37 \|\|

*iyaṃ māyāvatī bhāryā tanayasyāsya te satī \|*  
*śambarasya na bhāryeyaṃ śrūyatām atra kāraṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. This Māyāvatī is the chaste wife of your son. She is not the wife of Śambara. May the reason thereof be heard.

## \|\| 91.38 \|\|

*manmathe tu gate nāśaṃ tadudbhavaparāyaṇā \|*  
*śambaraṃ mohayām āsa māyārūpeṇa rukmiṇi \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O Rukmiṇī, when Cupid was killed, his wife eagerly waiting for his nativity, deluded Śambara by assuming an illusory form.

## \|\| 91.39 \|\|

*vivāhādyupabhogeṣu rūpaṃ māyāmayaṃ śubham \|*  
*darśayām āsa daityasya tasyeyaṃ madirekṣaṇā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. In the course of enjoyment of conjugal and other pleasures, this lady of charming eyes showed only the splendid illusory form to the asura.

## \|\| 91.40-42 \|\|

*kāmo 'vatīrṇaḥ putras te tasyeyaṃ dayitā ratiḥ \|*  
*viśaṅkā nātra kartavyā snuṣeyaṃ tava śobhanā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*tato harṣasamāviṣṭau rukmiṇīkeśavau tadā \|*  
*nagarī ca samastā sā sādhu sādhv ity abhāṣata \|\| 41 \|\|*

*ciraṃ naṣṭena putreṇa saṃgatāṃ prekṣya rukmiṇīm \|*  
*avāpa vismayaṃ sarvo dvāravatyāṃ janas tadā \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. Kāma has incarnated as your son. This is Rati his beloved wife. You need have no doubt about this. This is your splendid daughter-in-law.

## Chapter 92 - Rukmin is slain

## \|\| 92.1-2 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*cārudeṣṇaṃ sudeṣṇaṃ ca cārudehaṃ ca śobhanam \|*  
*suṣeṇaṃ cāruguptaṃ ca bhadracāruṃ tathāparam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*cāruvindaṃ sucāruṃ ca cāruṃ ca balināṃ varam \|*  
*rukmiṇy ajanayat putrān kanyāṃ cārumatīṃ tathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

1-2. Rukmiṇī gave birth to eight sons, viz. Cārudeṣṇa, Sudeṣṇa, Cārudeha, Suṣeṇa, Cārugupta, Bhadracāru, Cāruvinda (Cāruvindhya) and Cāru who was the most excellent among the strong ones.

She gave birth to a daughter Cārumatī also.

## \|\| 92.3-5 \|\|

*anyāś ca bhāryāḥ kṛṣṇasya babhūvuḥ sapta śobhanāḥ \|*  
*kālindī mitravindā ca satyā nāgnajitī tathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*devī jāmbavatī cāpi sadā tuṣṭā tu rohiṇī \|*  
*madrarājasutā cānyā suśīlā śīlamaṇḍalā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sātrājitī satyabhāmā lakṣmaṇā cāruhāsinī \|*  
*ṣoḍaśātra sahasrāṇi strīṇām anyāni cakriṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Kṛṣṇa had seven other splendid wives. They were: Kālindī, Mitravindā, Satyā the daughter of Nagnajit, the gentle lady Jāmbavatī who was always contented, Rohiṇī another virtuous daughter of Madra king with good conduct, Satyabhāmā the daughter of Satrājit and Lakṣmaṇā of sweet and beautiful smiles. The discus-bearing lord had sixteen thousand other wives.

## \|\| 92.6-7 \|\|

*pradyumno 'pi mahāvīryo rukmiṇas tanayāṃ śubhām \|*  
*svayaṃvarasthāṃ jagrāha sāpi taṃ tanayaṃ hareḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tasyām asyābhavat putro mahābalaparākramaḥ \|*  
*aniruddho raṇe ruddho vīryodadhir ariṃdamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Pradyumna of great vigour married the splendid daughter of Rukmin in a Svayaṃvara ceremony. She loved the son of Hari. Aniruddha of great strength and exploits was born of her. He was an ocean of prowess and a suppressor of enemies but he was held (treacherously in Mahābhārata) war.

## \|\| 92.8 \|\|

*tasyāpi rukmiṇaḥ pautrīṃ varayām āsa keśavaḥ \|*  
*dauhitrāya dadau rukmī spardhayann api śauriṇā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Kṛṣṇa chose the granddaughter of Rukmin as wife unto his grandson. Although Rukmin vied and contended with Kṛṣṇa he gave her to his daughter’s son (i.e. Aniruddha)

## \|\| 92.9 \|\|

*tasyā vivāhe rāmādyā yādavā hariṇā saha \|*  
*rukmiṇo nagaraṃ jagmur nāmnā bhojakaṭaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O brahmins, to attend her marriage Rāma and other descendants of Yadu went to Rukmin’s city named Bhojakaṭa, along with Lord Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 92.10 \|\|

*vivāhe tatra nirvṛtte prādyumneḥ sumahātmanaḥ \|*  
*kaliṅgarājapramukhā rukmiṇaṃ vākyam abruvan \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After the marriage of noble son of Pradyumna was concluded, Kaliṅga king and others spoke these words to Rukmin.

## \|\| 92.11 \|\|

*kaliṅgādaya ūcuḥ:*  
*anakṣajño halī dyūte tathāsya vyasanaṃ mahat \|*  
*tan nayāmo balaṃ tasmād dyūtenaiva mahādyute \|\| 11 \|\|*

Kaliṅga king and others said:

11\. Balarāma is not perfectly conversant with the game of dice; his indulgence in it is however, very great. Hence, O extremely lustrous one, we shall conquer him in the game of dice alone.

## \|\| 92.12 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*tatheti tān āha nṛpān rukmī balasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sabhāyāṃ saha rāmeṇa cakre dyūtaṃ ca vai tadā \|\| 12 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

12\. “So be it” said Rukmin who possessed great strength, to those kings. He played the game of dice with Rāma, in the assembly.

## \|\| 92.13 \|\|

*sahasram ekaṃ niṣkāṇāṃ rukmiṇā vijito balaḥ \|*  
*dvitīye divase cānyat sahasraṃ rukmiṇā jitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A stake of a thousand Niṣkas (gold coins) was won by Rukmin from Bala. On the second day another thousand was won by Rukmin.

## \|\| 92.14 \|\|

*tato daśa sahasrāṇi niṣkāṇāṃ paṇam ādade \|*  
*balabhadraprapannāni rukmī dyūtavidāṃ varaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then Rukmin the most excellent one among those who were conversant with the game of dice, put up a stake of ten thousand gold coins againts Baladeva who was desirous of victory.

## \|\| 92.15 \|\|

*tato jahāsātha balaṃ kaliṅgādhipatir dvijāḥ \|*  
*dantān vidarśayan mūḍho rukmī cāha madoddhataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then, O brahmins, exhibiting all his teeth, the foolish overlord of Kaliṅga laughed at Bala. The haughty Rukmin spoke then:

## \|\| 92.16 \|\|

*rukmy uvāca:*  
*avidyo 'yaṃ mahādyūte balabhadraḥ parājitaḥ \|*  
*mṛṣaivākṣāvalepatvād yo 'yaṃ mene 'kṣakovidam \|\| 16 \|\|*

Rukmin said:

16\. O members of the assembly, this Balarāma devoid of learning has been defeated by me in the game of dice. He is not conversant with either the manner of fighting or the lore of the game.

## \|\| 92.17 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā kaliṅgarājaṃ tu prakāśadaśanānanam \|*  
*rukmiṇaṃ cāpi durvākyaṃ kopaṃ cakre halāyudhaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

17\. On seeing the king of Kaliṅga with the teeth in his mouth fully exhibited, and Rukmin indulging in harsh words, Balarāma became infuriated.

## \|\| 92.18 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*tataḥ kopaparītātmā niṣkakoṭiṃ halāyudhaḥ \|*  
*glahaṃ jagrāha rukmī ca tatas tv akṣān apātayat \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. With his mind full of fury Balarāma put up the stake at a crore of gold coins. Rukmin too accepted it. He threw the dice for that purpose.

## \|\| 92.19 \|\|

*ajayad baladevo 'tha prāhoccais taṃ jitaṃ mayā \|*  
*mameti rukmī prāhoccair alīkoktair alaṃ balam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Baladeva won the stake. He said to him loudly “This is won by me”.

“The victory is mine” loudly proclaimed Rukmin to Bala in false words.

## \|\| 92.20 \|\|

*tvayokto 'yaṃ glahaḥ satyaṃ na mamaiṣo 'numoditaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ tvayā ced vijitaṃ na mayā vijitaṃ katham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “It is true that this stake was announced by you. But it had not been accepted or approved of by me. That being the case if (you say) you have won how (can’t I say that) I have won?

## \|\| 92.21 \|\|

*tato 'ntarikṣe vāg uccaiḥ prāha gambhīranādinī \|*  
*baladevasya taṃ kopaṃ vardhayantī mahātmanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then loud resonant words rose up in the sky aggravating the fury of noble Baladeva.

## \|\| 92.22 \|\|

*ākāśavāg uvāca:*  
*jitaṃ tu baladevena rukmiṇā bhāṣitaṃ mṛṣā \|*  
*anuktvā vacanaṃ kiṃcit kṛtaṃ bhavati karmaṇā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The speech in the firmament said: “The stake is won by Baladeva. What is uttered by Rukmin is false. Certain things are accepted through actions even without mentioning words.”

## \|\| 92.23 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*tato balaḥ samutthāya krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ \|*  
*jaghānāṣṭāpadenaiva rukmiṇaṃ sa mahābalaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

23\. Then Bala of great strength got up with his eyes turned red due to fury. With the dice board itself he hit and killed Rukmin.

## \|\| 92.24 \|\|

*kaliṅgarājaṃ cādāya visphurantaṃ balād balaḥ \|*  
*babhañja dantān kupito yaiḥ prakāśaṃ jahāsa saḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. With great force he held the king of Kaliṅga who was throbbing and trembling. In his fury he broke his teeth with which he had openly laughed at him;

## \|\| 92.25 \|\|

*ākṛṣya ca mahāstambhaṃ jātarūpamayaṃ balaḥ \|*  
*jaghāna ye tatpakṣās tān bhūbhṛtaḥ kupito balaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The infuriated Bala seized a great column of gold and killed those kings who belonged to his side.

## \|\| 92.26 \|\|

*tato hāhākṛtaṃ sarvaṃ palāyanaparaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*tad rājamaṇḍalaṃ sarvaṃ babhūva kupite bale \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. When Bala was angry thus, O brahmins, the entire assembly of kings became eager to flee crying out “Alas, Alas”.

## \|\| 92.27 \|\|

*balena nihataṃ śrutvā rukmiṇaṃ madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*novāca vacanaṃ kiṃcid rukmiṇībalayor bhayāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On hearing that Rukmin was killed by Bala, Kṛṣṇa did not utter a single word for fear of offending Rukmiṇī or Bala.

## \|\| 92.28 \|\|

*tato 'niruddham ādāya kṛtodvāhaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*dvārakām ājagāmātha yaducakraṃ sakeśavam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then, O excellent brahmins, the descendants of Yadu, accompanied by Kṛṣṇa returned to Dvārakā taking Aniruddha with them after his marriage rites were concluded.

## Chapter 93 - Naraka is killed

## \|\| 93.1-2 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*dvāravatyāṃ tataḥ śauriṃ śakras tribhuvaneśvaraḥ \|*  
*ājagāmātha munayo mattairāvatapṛṣṭhagaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*praviśya dvārakāṃ so 'tha samīpe ca hares tadā \|*  
*kathayām āsa daityasya narakasya viceṣṭitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

1-2. O sages, seated on the back of the inebriated Airāvata, Indra the lord of the three worlds came to meet Lord Kṛṣṇa at Dvāravatī. After entering the city he approached the lord and mentioned to him the vicious activities of the asura Naraka.

## \|\| 93.3 \|\|

*indra uvāca:*  
*tvayā nāthena devānāṃ manuṣyatve 'pi tiṣṭhatā \|*  
*praśamaṃ sarvaduḥkhāni nītāni madhusūdana \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O lord, all miseries have been subdued by you, the lord of Devas, though stationed in the form of a human being.

## \|\| 93.4-5 \|\|

*tapasvijanarakṣāyai so 'riṣṭo dhenukas tathā \|*  
*pralambādyās tathā keśī te sarve nihatās tvayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kaṃsaḥ kuvalayāpīḍaḥ pūtanā bālaghātinī \|*  
*nāśaṃ nītās tvayā sarve ye 'nye jagadupadravāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. For affording protection to those people who perform penance, the following asuras have been killed by you—Ariṣṭa, Dhenuka, Keśin, Pralamba and others. Those who harassed the universe were destroyed by you, namely, Kaṃsa, Kuvalayāpīḍa, the child-slayer Pūtanā and many others.

## \|\| 93.6 \|\|

*yuṣmaddordaṇḍasaṃbuddhi- paritrāte jagattraye \|*  
*yajñe yajñahaviḥ prāśya tṛptiṃ yānti divaukasaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. When the three worlds have been saved by your excellent intellect as well as brawny baton-like arms, the heaven-dwellers partook of oblations in the sacrifice and became gratified.

## \|\| 93.7 \|\|

*so 'haṃ sāṃpratam āyāto yannimittaṃ janārdana \|*  
*tac chrutvā tatpratīkāra- prayatnaṃ kartum arhasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O lord, it behoves you to pursue efforts and countermeasures after listening to the reason for which I have come now.

## \|\| 93.8 \|\|

*bhaumo 'yaṃ narako nāma prāgjyotiṣapureśvaraḥ \|*  
*karoti sarvabhūtānām apaghātam ariṃdama \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. O suppressor of enemies, this son of Bhūmi named Naraka who is the king of Prāgjyotiṣa harasses and destroys all living beings.

## \|\| 93.9 \|\|

*devasiddhasurādīnāṃ nṛpāṇāṃ ca janārdana \|*  
*hatvā tu so 'suraḥ kanyā rurodha nijamandire \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After killing Devas, Siddhas, kings, and others, that Asura imprisoned their daughters in his own palace.

## \|\| 93.10 \|\|

*chattraṃ yat salilasrāvi taj jahāra pracetasaḥ \|*  
*mandarasya tathā śṛṅgaṃ hṛtavān maṇiparvatam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He has taken away the umbrella of Pracetas, that exudes water. He has removed the Maṇiparvata, peak of the Mandara.

## \|\| 93.11 \|\|

*amṛtasrāviṇī divye mātur me 'mṛtakuṇḍale \|*  
*jahāra so 'suro 'dityā vāñchaty airāvataṃ dvipam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. That Asura has taken away the illustrious ear-rings of my mother Aditi, the ear-rings that exude nectar. He now desires to take possession of my elephant Airāvata.

## \|\| 93.12 \|\|

*durnītam etad govinda mayā tasya tavoditam \|*  
*yad atra pratikartavyaṃ tat svayaṃ parimṛśyatām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O lord, I have told you about his evil activities. What steps should be taken by way of remedy may be pondered over by yourself.

## \|\| 93.13 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*iti śrutvā smitaṃ kṛtvā bhagavān devakīsutaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā vāsavaṃ haste samuttasthau varāsanāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

13\. On hearing this, lord Kṛṣṇa, son of Devakī, smiled and caught hold of the hand of Indra. He then got up from the excellent seat.

## \|\| 93.14 \|\|

*saṃcintitam upāruhya garuḍaṃ gaganecaram \|*  
*satyabhāmāṃ samāropya yayau prāgjyotiṣaṃ puram \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He then rode on Garuḍa who traversed through the sky. He kept Satyabhāmā also on its back and went to the city of Prāgjyotiṣa.

## \|\| 93.15 \|\|

*āruhyairāvataṃ nāgaṃ śakro 'pi tridaśālayam \|*  
*tato jagāma sumanāḥ paśyatāṃ dvārakaukasām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Even as the residents of Dvārakā watched him, the delighted Indra mounted his elephant Airāvata and went to heaven.

## \|\| 93.16 \|\|

*prāgjyotiṣapurasyāsya samantāc chatayojanam \|*  
*ācitaṃ bhairavaiḥ pāśaiḥ parasainyanivāraṇe \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. For a hundred Yojanas all round the city of Prāgjyotiṣa, the entire place was covered with terrible nooses in order to ward off the army of enemies.

## \|\| 93.17 \|\|

*tāṃś ciccheda hariḥ pāśān kṣiptvā cakraṃ sudarśanam \|*  
*tato muraḥ samuttasthau taṃ jaghāna ca keśavaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Lord Kṛṣṇa hurled his discus Sudarśana and cut off those nooses. Then the asura Mura got up. Keśava killed him.

## \|\| 93.18 \|\|

*muros tu tanayān sapta sahasrās tāṃs tato hariḥ \|*  
*cakradhārāgninirdagdhāṃś cakāra śalabhān iva \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. By the fire from the sharp edges of his discus Hari burned seven thousand sons of Mura as though they were mere moths.

## \|\| 93.19 \|\|

*hatvā muraṃ hayagrīvaṃ tathā pañcajanaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*prāgjyotiṣapuraṃ dhīmāṃs tvarāvān samupādravat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O brahmins, after killing Mura, Hayagriva and Pañcajana the intelligent lord hastened to Prāgjyotiṣa.

## \|\| 93.20 \|\|

*narakenāsya tatrābhūn mahāsainyena saṃyugaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇasya yatra govindo jaghne daityān sahasraśaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. There Kṛṣṇa fought with Naraka who had a great army. In that battle Lord Kṛṣṇa killed thousands of asuras.

## \|\| 93.21 \|\|

*śastrāstravarṣaṃ muñcantaṃ sa bhaumaṃ narakaṃ balī \|*  
*kṣiptvā cakraṃ dvidhā cakre cakrī daiteyacakrahā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By hurling his discus the discus-bearing lord, the powerful destroyer of asuras, split Naraka into two, Naraka, son of the Earth, who was hurling weapons and missiles on him.

## \|\| 93.22 \|\|

*hate tu narake bhūmir gṛhītvāditikuṇḍale \|*  
*upatasthe jagannāthaṃ vākyaṃ cedam athābravīt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When Naraka was killed, the Earth approached the lord of the universe taking with her the earrings of Aditi. She spoke these words:—

## \|\| 93.23 \|\|

*dharaṇy uvāca:*  
*yadāham uddhṛtā nātha tvayā śūkaramūrtinā \|*  
*tvatsaṃsparśabhavaḥ putras tadāyaṃ mayy ajāyata \|\| 23 \|\|*

The Earth said:

23\. O lord, when I was lifted up by you in the form of a Boar, this son had been born of me as a result of my contact with you.

## \|\| 93.24 \|\|

*so 'yaṃ tvayaiva datto me tvayaiva vinipātitaḥ \|*  
*gṛhāṇa kuṇḍale ceme pālayāsya ca saṃtatim \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He had been given to me by you and now has been struck down by you. Take back these two ear-rings and protect his children.

## \|\| 93.25 \|\|

*bhārāvataraṇārthāya mamaiva bhagavān imam \|*  
*aṃśena lokam āyātaḥ prasādasumukha prabho \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. It is for reducing my own burden that O lord of gentle and pleasant face, you have come to this worlds a part of yours.

## \|\| 93.26 \|\|

*tvaṃ kartā ca vikartā ca saṃhartā prabhavo 'vyayaḥ \|*  
*jagatsvarūpo yaś ca tvaṃ stūyase 'cyuta kiṃ mayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. You are the creator, re-creator, annihilator, eternal source of origin and one whose form is identical with that of the universe. O Acyuta, how am I to eulogise you?

## \|\| 93.27 \|\|

*vyāpī vyāpyaḥ kriyā kartā kāryaṃ ca bhagavān sadā \|*  
*sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā stūyase 'cyuta kiṃ mayā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. You are the one all-pervading and the pervaded; deed, the doer and the thing done. You are the Ātman, the inner soul of all living beings. O Acyuta, how can I eulogise you?

## \|\| 93.28 \|\|

*paramātmā tvam ātmā ca bhūtātmā cāvyayo bhavān \|*  
*yadā tadā stutir nāsti kimarthaṃ te pravartatām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. You are the Supreme Ātman, the innermost soul, the soul of living beings, the eternal lord. These are not your praises. They are the statements of facts. How shall anyone go about (this act of eulogy)?

## \|\| 93.29 \|\|

*prasīda sarvabhūtātman narakena kṛtaṃ ca yat \|*  
*tat kṣamyatām adoṣāya matsutaḥ sa nipātitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O lord, the soul of all-living beings, be pleased. May What is done by Naraka be excused for making him free from defects. My son has already been struck down.

## \|\| 93.30 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*tatheti coktvā dharaṇīṃ bhagavān bhūtabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*ratnāni narakāvāsāj jagrāha munisattamāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

30\. “So be it”, the lord said to the Earth. O excellent sages, the conceiver and creator of the living beings took up jewels from the residence of Naraka.

## \|\| 93.31 \|\|

*kanyāpure sa kanyānāṃ ṣoḍaśātulavikramaḥ \|*  
*śatādhikāni dadṛśe sahasrāṇi dvijottamāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The lord of unequalled exploits saw sixteen thousand one hundred virgins in the harem, O excellent brahmins.

## \|\| 93.32-35 \|\|

*caturdaṃṣṭrān gajāṃś cogrān ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi dṛṣṭavān \|*  
*kāmbojānāṃ tathāśvānāṃ niyutāny ekaviṃśatim \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kanyās tāś ca tathā nāgāṃs tān aśvān dvārakāṃ purīm \|*  
*prāpayām āsa govindaḥ sadyo narakakiṃkaraiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*dadṛśe vāruṇaṃ chattraṃ tathaiva maṇiparvatam \|*  
*āropayām āsa harir garuḍe patageśvare \|\| 34 \|\|*

*āruhya ca svayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ satyabhāmāsahāyavān \|*  
*adityāḥ kuṇḍale dātuṃ jagāma tridaśālayam \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. He saw six thousand terrible elephants with four tusks and two million and one hundred thousand Kamboja horses. Immediately the lord despatched those girls, elephants and horses to Dvārakā through the servants of Naraka. The umbrella of Varuṇa and the jewel mountain were put on the back of Garuḍa the lord of birds. Accompanied by Satyabhāmā, Kṛṣṇa mounted Garuḍa and went to Heaven to restore ear-rings to Aditi.

## Chapter 94 - The prayer by Indra

## \|\| 94.1 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*garuḍo vāruṇaṃ chattraṃ tathaiva maṇiparvatam \|*  
*sabhāryaṃ ca hṛṣīkeśaṃ līlayaiva vahan yayau \|\| 1 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

1\. Playfully carrying the umbrella of Varuṇa, the jewel mountain and bearing lord Kṛṣṇa on his back accompanied by his wife, Garuḍa went ahead.

## \|\| 94.2 \|\|

*tataḥ śaṅkham upādhmāya svargadvāraṃ gato hariḥ \|*  
*upatasthus tato devāḥ sārghapātrā janārdanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Lord Kṛṣṇa reached the gateway of heaven and blew the conch. Then Devas approached the lord along with the vessels full of materials of worship.

## \|\| 94.3 \|\|

*sa devair arcitaḥ kṛṣṇo devamātur niveśanam \|*  
*sitābhraśikharākāraṃ praviśya dadṛśe 'ditim \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After being worshipped by Devas, Kṛṣṇa entered the abode of the mother of Devas that had the shape of the peak of white mountain. After entering it he saw Aditi.

## \|\| 94.4 \|\|

*sa tāṃ praṇamya śakreṇa sahitaḥ kuṇḍalottame \|*  
*dadau narakanāśaṃ ca śaśaṃsāsyai janārdanaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Accompanied by Indra he bowed to her. The lord gave her the excellent earrings and intimated to her the death of Naraka.

## \|\| 94.5 \|\|

*tataḥ prītā jaganmātā dhātāraṃ jagatāṃ harim \|*  
*tuṣṭāvāditir avyagraṃ kṛtvā tatpravaṇaṃ manaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then Aditi the mother of Devas was pleased. Unruffled, she directed her mind to the lord who is the creator of the worlds and eulogised him.

## \|\| 94.6 \|\|

*aditir uvāca:*  
*namas te puṇḍarīkākṣa bhaktānām abhayaṃkara \|*  
*sanātanātman bhūtātman sarvātman bhūtabhāvana \|\| 6 \|\|*

Aditi said:

6\. Obeisance to you, O lotus-eyed one, O lord causing fearlessness to devotees, O lord, the eternal Ātman, O Ātman of living beings, O Ātman of everything, O creator of living beings.

## \|\| 94.7-10 \|\|

*praṇetar manaso buddher indriyāṇāṃ guṇātmaka \|*  
*sitadīrghādiniḥśeṣa- kalpanāparivarjita \|\| 7 \|\|*

*janmādibhir asaṃspṛṣṭa- svapnādivārivarjitaḥ \|*  
*saṃdhyā rātrir ahar bhūmir gaganaṃ vāyur ambu ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*hutāśano mano buddhir bhūtādis tvaṃ tathācyuta \|*  
*sṛṣṭisthitivināśānāṃ kartā kartṛpatir bhavān \|\| 9 \|\|*

*brahmaviṣṇuśivākhyābhir ātmamūrtibhir īśvaraḥ \|*  
*māyābhir etad vyāptaṃ te jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. You are of the nature of vital airs, soul and mind, intellect and sense-organs. You are beyond three attributes. O pure one, you are devoid of mutually clashing opposites. O lord stationed in the heart of all, O lord devoid of all conceptions such as those of whiteness, and length. You are untouched by birth, You are devoid of dreamy state. You are all these—dusk, night, day, Earth, firmament, wind, water, fire, mind, intellect and subtle elements. You are Acyuta, the cause of creation, sustenance and destruction; you are the lord of makers and doers. With your forms named Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva, you are the lord of all. This universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings is pervaded by your Māyā.

## \|\| 94.11 \|\|

*anātmany ātmavijñānaṃ sā te māyā janārdana \|*  
*ahaṃ mameti bhāvo 'tra yayā samupajāyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O lord, if one takes the non-Ātman to be the Ātman, this misconception is your Māyā. It is from this that the ideas of ‘I’, ‘Mine’ etc. emerge.

## \|\| 94.12-19 \|\|

*saṃsāramadhye māyāyās tavaitan nātha ceṣṭitam \|*  
*yaiḥ svadharmaparair nātha narair ārādhito bhavān \|\| 12 \|\|*

*te taranty akhilām etāṃ māyām ātmavimuktaye \|*  
*brahmādyāḥ sakalā devā manuṣyāḥ paśavas tathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*viṣṇumāyāmahāvarte mohāndhatamasāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*ārādhya tvām abhīpsante kāmān ātmabhavakṣaye \|\| 14 \|\|*

*pade te puruṣā baddhā māyayā bhagavaṃs tava \|*  
*mayā tvaṃ putrakāminyā vairipakṣakṣayāya ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ārādhito na mokṣāya māyāvilasitaṃ hi tat \|*  
*kaupīnācchādanaprāyā vāñchā kalpadrumād api \|\| 16 \|\|*

*jāyate yad apuṇyānāṃ so 'parādhaḥ svadoṣajaḥ \|*  
*tat prasīdākhilajagan- māyāmohakarāvyaya \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ajñānaṃ jñānasadbhāva bhūtabhūteśa nāśaya \|*  
*namas te cakrahastāya śārṅgahastāya te namaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*gadāhastāya te viṣṇo śaṅkhahastāya te namaḥ \|*  
*etat paśyāmi te rūpaṃ sthūlacihnopaśobhitam \|*  
*na jānāmi paraṃ yat te prasīda parameśvara \|\| 19 \|\|*

12-19. O lord, this is the activity of your Māyā amid the ocean of worldly existence.

Those men who are devoted to their own Dharmas and by whom you have been propitiated, surmount all this Māyā and proceed to self-liberation.

Brahmā and Devas, human beings and animals are enveloped by the darkness of delusion. They are involved in the great whirlpool of your Māyā.

O lord, these men bound by your Māyā desire to obtain all desires when rebirths of the Ātman cease, after propitiating you.

You were propitiated by me with a longing for sons and for the extermination of the hosts of foes. It was not for liberation. Indeed, it is the activity of Māyā.

It is like the longing for loin-cloth and similar things from the wish-yielding Kalpa tree. This kind of guilt happens in the case of those who perform meritorious deeds deriving worldly fruits. It originates from their own defects.

Hence, be pleased, O unchanging lord, who cause illusory delusion into the entire universe. Destroy our ignorance, O lord of all living beings having perfect knowledge and good intention.

Obeisance to you, to the discus-armed one, obeisance to you who have the conch in your hand. Obeisance to the deity holding the ironclub. O Viṣṇu, obeisance to you, having lotus in your hand.

I see your form rendered splendid by gross signs and symbols. I do not know the greatest principle. O Supreme lord be pleased.

## \|\| 94.20-23 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*adityaivaṃ stuto viṣṇuḥ prahasyāha surāraṇim \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca:*  
*mātā devi tvam asmākaṃ prasīda varadā bhava \|\| 21 \|\|*

*aditir uvāca:*  
*evam astu yathecchā te tvam aśeṣasurāsuraiḥ \|*  
*ajeyaḥ puruṣavyāghra martyaloke bhaviṣyasi \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*tato 'nantaram evāsya śakrāṇīsahitāṃ ditim \|*  
*satyabhāmā praṇamyāha prasīdeti punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

20-23. Thus eulogised by Aditi the lord laughed and spoke to Aditi.

## \|\| 94.24 \|\|

*aditir uvāca:*  
*matprasādān na te subhru jarā vairūpyam eva ca \|*  
*bhaviṣyaty anavadyāṅgi sarvakāmā bhaviṣyasi \|\| 24 \|\|*

Śrīkṛṣṇa said:

O gentle lady, you are our mother. Be pleased. Be one that bestows boons.

Aditi said:

Let it be as you wish. O tiger among men, you will be unconquerable by Devas, Asuras and human beings.

Vyāsa said:

Immediately thereafter, Satyabhāmā accompanied by Śacī bowed to Aditi and said again and again—‘Be pleased’.

Aditi said:

24\. O lady of fine eye-brows, due to my favour you will never have old age or deformity. O lady of blameless limbs, you will enjoy all worldly pleasures.

## \|\| 94.25 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*adityā tu kṛtānujño devarājo janārdanam \|*  
*yathāvat pūjayām āsa bahumānapuraḥsaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

25\. Permitted by Aditi, the king of Devas duly worshipped the lord with adequate reverence.

## \|\| 94.26 \|\|

*tato dadarśa kṛṣṇo 'pi satyabhāmāsahāyavān \|*  
*devodyānāni sarvāṇi nandanādīni sattamāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then, O excellent ones, Kṛṣṇa accompanied by Satyabhāmā visited the divine gardens and parks such as Nandana.

## \|\| 94.27-28 \|\|

*dadarśa ca sugandhāḍhyaṃ mañjarīpuñjadhāriṇam \|*  
*śaityāhlādakaraṃ divyaṃ tāmrapallavaśobhitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*mathyamāne 'mṛte jātaṃ jātarūpasamaprabham \|*  
*pārijātaṃ jagannāthaḥ keśavaḥ keśisūdanaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha govindaṃ satyabhāmā dvijottamāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. There Keśava, the lord of the Universe, the destroyer of Keśin saw the Pārijāta tree which put forth bunches of excessively fragrant flowers, which was divine, which caused cool comfort and delight, which was beautified by tender sprouts, which had the lustre similar to that of gold and which was produced when the milk ocean was churned for getting nectar.

O excellent brahmins, on seeing the Pārijāta tree, Satyabhāmā spoke to the lord.

## \|\| 94.29-32 \|\|

*satyabhāmovāca:*  
*kasmān na dvārakām eṣa nīyate kṛṣṇa pādapaḥ \|*  
*yadi te tad vacaḥ satyaṃ satyātyarthaṃ priyeti me \|\| 29 \|\|*

*madgṛhe niṣkuṭārthāya tad ayaṃ nīyatāṃ taruḥ \|*  
*na me jāmbavatī tādṛg abhīṣṭā na ca rukmiṇī \|\| 30 \|\|*

*satye yathā tvam ity uktaṃ tvayā kṛṣṇāsakṛt priyam \|*  
*satyaṃ tad yadi govinda nopacārakṛtaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tad astu pārijāto 'yaṃ mama gehavibhūṣaṇam \|*  
*bibhratī pārijātasya keśapāśena mañjarīm \|*  
*sapatnīnām ahaṃ madhye śobheyam iti kāmaye \|\| 32 \|\|*

Satyabhāmā said:

29-32. O Kṛṣṇa, why is not this tree taken to Dvārakā?

If these words of yours are true—“Satyā is my most beloved one”, let this tree be taken to my house for beautifying my garden. O Kṛṣṇa, these pleasing words are often mentioned by you to me—“O Satyā, neither Jāmbavatī nor Rukmiṇī is so much desired by me as you are”. If, O lord, those are not mere complimentary flattering words, if they are really meant, let this Pārijāta be an ornament to my house.

I shall appear very splendid amongst my co-wives if I wear the bunch of its flowers on my braid of hair. Hence I desire for It.

## \|\| 94.33 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*ity uktaḥ sa prahasyainaṃ pārijātaṃ garutmati \|*  
*āropayām āsa haris tam ūcur vanarakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

33\. The lord who was requested thus laughingly placed the Pārijāta tree on Garuḍa. Then the guards of the park said.

## \|\| 94.34 \|\|

*vanapālā ūcuḥ:*  
*bhoḥ śacī devarājasya mahiṣī tatparigraham \|*  
*pārijātaṃ na govinda hartum arhasi pādapam \|\| 34 \|\|*

The guards of the park said:

34\. O lord, Śacī is the crowned queen of Devas. It does not behove you to take away the Pārijāta tree specially adopted by her.

## \|\| 94.35 \|\|

*śacīvibhūṣaṇārthāya devair amṛtamanthane \|*  
*utpādito 'yaṃ na kṣemī gṛhītvainaṃ gamiṣyasi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. When the milk ocean was being churned for obtaining nectar, this tree had been adopted by Devas for embellishing Śacī. If you take this, you will not go safe and secure.

## \|\| 94.36 \|\|

*mauḍhyāt prārthayase kṣemī gṛhītvainaṃ ca ko vrajet \|*  
*avaśyam asya devendro vikṛtiṃ kṛṣṇa yāsyati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. You seek for this Pārijāta out of foolishness. Who will go out safe and secure if he takes this with him? O Kṛṣṇa, the lord of Devas will indeed be furious over this.

## \|\| 94.37 \|\|

*vajrodyatakaraṃ śakram anuyāsyanti cāmarāḥ \|*  
*tad alaṃ sakalair devair vigraheṇa tavācyuta \|*  
*vipākakaṭu yat karma na tac chaṃsanti paṇḍitāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The immortal ones will follow Indra with the thunderbolt raised up in his hand. Hence, O Acyuta, enough of your attempts to quarrel with Devas. Scholars do not praise that action which is very bitter in its result.

## \|\| 94.38-44 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*ity ukte tair uvācaitān satyabhāmātikopinī \|\| 38 \|\|*

*satyabhāmovāca:*  
*kā śacī pārijātasya ko vā śakraḥ surādhipaḥ \|*  
*sāmānyaḥ sarvalokānāṃ yady eṣo 'mṛtamanthane \|\| 39 \|\|*

*samutpannaḥ purā kasmād eko gṛhṇāti vāsavaḥ \|*  
*yathā surā yathā cendur yathā śrīr vanarakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sāmānyaḥ sarvalokasya pārijātas tathā drumaḥ \|*  
*bhartṛbāhumahāgarvād ruṇaddhy enam atho śacī \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tat kathyatāṃ drutaṃ gatvā paulomyā vacanaṃ mama \|*  
*satyabhāmā vadaty evaṃ bhartṛgarvoddhatākṣaram \|\| 42 \|\|*

*yadi tvaṃ dayitā bhartur yadi tasya priyā hy asi \|*  
*madbhartur harato vṛkṣaṃ tat kāraya nivāraṇam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*jānāmi te patiṃ śakraṃ jānāmi tridaśeśvaram \|*  
*pārijātaṃ tathāpy enaṃ mānuṣī hārayāmi te \|\| 44 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

38-44. When this was mentioned by him, the infuriated Satyabhāmā said:—

## \|\| 94.45 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*ity uktā rakṣiṇo gatvā proccaiḥ procur yathoditam \|*  
*śacī cotsāhayām āsa tridaśādhipatiṃ patim \|\| 45 \|\|*

Satyabhāmā said:

Who is Śacī and who is Indra the lord of Devas, in regard to this Pārijāta tree? This Pārijāta tree is common to the worlds. It originated formerly (as common to all). Why should Indra alone take it? Just like the wine, moon or Śrī, O guards of the park, this tree born of the ocean is common to all.

If Śacī clings to this, on account of her pride in the mighty arms of her husband, go quickly to her and mention these words—Satyabhāmā says in words couched in her pride over her husband, “If you are the beloved of your husband, if you are fond of him, prevent my husband from removing this tree, I know your husband Indra. I know the lord of Devas. Still I, a human being, shall remove this Pārijāta.”

Vyāsa said:

45\. The guards of the park who were addressed thus, went to Śacī and told her what they were told. Śacī then encouraged her husband the over-lord of Devas.

## \|\| 94.46 \|\|

*tataḥ samastadevānāṃ sainyaiḥ parivṛto harim \|*  
*pravṛktaḥ pārijātārtham indro yodhayituṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Then, O brahmins, Indra who was surrounded by the armies of Devas began to fight over the Pārijāta tree.

## \|\| 94.47 \|\|

*tataḥ parighanistriṃśa- gadāśūladharāyudhāḥ \|*  
*babhūvus tridaśāḥ sajjāḥ śakre vajrakare sthite \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Then Indra stood ready with the thunderbolt in his hand. Devas also stood in readiness holding their weapons such as iron clubs, sword and tridents.

## \|\| 94.48-50 \|\|

*tato nirīkṣya govindo nāgarājopari sthitam \|*  
*śakraṃ devaparīvāraṃ yuddhāya samupasthitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*cakāra śaṅkhanirghoṣaṃ diśaḥ śabdena pūrayan \|*  
*mumoca ca śaravrātaṃ sahasrāyutasaṃmitam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tato diśo nabhaś caiva dṛṣṭvā śaraśatācitam \|*  
*mumucus tridaśāḥ sarve śastrāṇy astrāṇy anekaśaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. On seeing Indra seated on his lordly elephant, surrounded by Devas and approaching him for a battle, the lord blew on his conch. He filled the quarters with sounds. He discharged thousands and ten thousands of arrows. On seeing the quarters and the firmament covered with hundreds of arrows, Devas discharged many missiles and weapons.

## \|\| 94.51 \|\|

*ekaikam astraṃ śastraṃ ca devair muktaṃ sahasradhā \|*  
*ciccheda līlayaiveśo jagatāṃ madhusūdanaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then lord of the worlds playfully split each of the missiles and weapons discharged by Devas, into a thousand bits.

## \|\| 94.52 \|\|

*pāśaṃ salilarājasya samākṛṣyoragāśanaḥ \|*  
*cacāla khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛttvā bālapannagadehavat \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Garuḍa snatched the noose of the king of waters (i.e. Varuṇa), split it into bits like the body of a young serpent and moved about.

## \|\| 94.53 \|\|

*yamena prahitaṃ daṇḍaṃ gadāprakṣepakhaṇḍitam \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ pātayām āsa bhagavān devakīsutaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The lord, the son of Devakī, struck down on to the ground the staff discharged by Yama. It was broken when he hurled his iron club at it.

## \|\| 94.54 \|\|

*śibikāṃ ca dhaneśasya cakreṇa tilaśo vibhuḥ \|*  
*cakāra śaurir arkendū dṛṣṭipātahataujasau \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The lord Kṛṣṇa smashed the palanquin of the god of wealth into minute bits like gingelly seeds. The sun and the moon lost their prowess as it was destroyed by a single glance of the lord.

## \|\| 94.55 \|\|

*nīto 'gniḥ śataśo bāṇair drāvitā vasavo diśaḥ \|*  
*cakravicchinnaśūlāgrā rudrā bhuvi nipātitāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The fire god was split into hundreds by means of arrows. The Vasus were made to flee in all directions. The tips of the tridents of Rudras were split by the discus and the Rudras themselves were struck down on to the ground.

## \|\| 94.56 \|\|

*sādhyā viśve ca maruto gandharvāś caiva sāyakaiḥ \|*  
*śārṅgiṇā preritāḥ sarve vyomni śālmalitūlavat \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The Sādhyas, Viśvedevas, Maruts and Gandharvas were sent up into the sky like the cotton bits from a Śālmali tree by the Śārṅga-bearing lord through his arrows.

## \|\| 94.57 \|\|

*garuḍaś cāpi vaktreṇa pakṣābhyāṃ ca nakhāṅkuraiḥ \|*  
*bhakṣayann ahanad devān dānavāṃś ca sadā khagaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Garuḍa killed and ate Devas and Upadevas by means of his beak, wings and claws.

## \|\| 94.58 \|\|

*tataḥ śarasahasreṇa devendramadhusūdanau \|*  
*parasparaṃ vavarṣāte dhārābhir iva toyadau \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Then Indra, the lord of Devas, and lord Kṛṣṇa, the slayer of Madhu showered each other with a thousand arrows like two clouds by heavy downpours.

## \|\| 94.59 \|\|

*airāvatena garuḍo yuyudhe tatra saṃkule \|*  
*devaiḥ sametair yuyudhe śakreṇa ca janārdanaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In the utter confusion obtaining there, Garuḍa fought with Airāvata and lord Kṛṣṇa with Devas accompanied by Indra.

## \|\| 94.60 \|\|

*chinneṣu śīryamāṇeṣu śastreṣv astreṣu satvaram \|*  
*jagrāha vāsavo vajraṃ kṛṣṇaś cakraṃ sudarśanam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. When weapons and missiles were split and scattered, Indra hastily seized the thunderbolt and Kṛṣṇa took up his discus Sudarśana.

## \|\| 94.61 \|\|

*tato hāhākṛtaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*vajracakradharau dṛṣṭvā devarājajanārdanau \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. On seeing the king of Devas and Śrī Kṛṣṇa holding up their thunderbolt and discus respectively the whole of the universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings raised a hue and cry.

## \|\| 94.62 \|\|

*kṣiptaṃ vajram athendreṇa jagrāha bhagavān hariḥ \|*  
*na mumoca tadā cakraṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Lord Kṛṣṇa caught hold of thunderbolt hurled by Indra. Without releasing his discus he told him ‘stay, stay’.

## \|\| 94.63 \|\|

*pranaṣṭavajraṃ devendraṃ garuḍakṣatavāhanam \|*  
*satyabhāmābravīd vākyaṃ palāyanaparāyaṇam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. As the king of Devas lost his thunderbolt, as his vehicle was wounded by Garuḍa, he became inclined to run away then. Satyabhāmā spoke to him.

## \|\| 94.64 \|\|

*satyabhāmovāca:*  
*trailokyeśvara no yuktaṃ śacībhartuḥ palāyanam \|*  
*pārijātasragābhogāt tvām upasthāsyate śacī \|\| 64 \|\|*

Satyabhāmā said:

64\. O lord of three worlds, it is not proper for the husband of Śacī to run away. Śacī will honour you with a big garland of Pārijāta flowers.

## \|\| 94.65 \|\|

*kīdṛśaṃ deva rājyaṃ te pārijātasragujjvalām \|*  
*apaśyato yathāpūrvaṃ praṇayābhyāgatāṃ śacīm \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Of what nature is your divine realm? You are unable to see Śacī approaching you lovingly as before shining with the Pārijāta garlands.

## \|\| 94.66 \|\|

*alaṃ śakra prayāsena na vrīḍāṃ yātum arhasi \|*  
*nīyatāṃ pārijāto 'yaṃ devāḥ santu gatavyathāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. O Indra, enough of your endeavour. It does not behove you to be ashamed. Let this Pārijāta tree be taken away. Let Devas be rid of pain.

## \|\| 94.67 \|\|

*patigarvāvalepena bahumānapuraḥsaram \|*  
*na dadarśa gṛhāyātām upacāreṇa māṃ śacī \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. On account of her excessive pride and arrogance Śacī did not view me with reverence as I went to her house. Nor did she honour me.

## \|\| 94.68 \|\|

*strītvād agurucittāhaṃ svabhartuḥ ślāghanāparā \|*  
*tataḥ kṛtavatī śakra bhavatā saha vigraham \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Being a woman, my mind is very light. I was devoted to the praise of my husband. Therefore, O Indra I picked up a quarrel with you.

## \|\| 94.69 \|\|

*tad alaṃ pārijātena parasvena hṛtena vā \|*  
*rūpeṇa yaśasā caiva bhavet strī kā na garvitā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Hence, enough of this Pārijāta which is another man’s property. Why should it be taken away? Which woman does not become proud due to beauty and fame.

## \|\| 94.70 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca:*  
*ity ukte vai nivavṛte devarājas tayā dvijāḥ \|*  
*prāha cainām alaṃ caṇḍi sakhi khedātivistaraiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

Vyāsa said:

70\. O brahmins, when addressed thus the king of Devas returned and said to her:
